## #275 [Bug] TMOV FP32 to FP16 is supported by PTO-ISA C++, but fails at MLIR verify()

- State: closed
- URL: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/PTOAS/issues/275
- Created: 2026-03-16T10:11:34Z
- Updated: 2026-03-16T15:42:54Z
- Closed: 2026-03-16T15:42:54Z

### Body

### Component

Verifier / IR semantics (lib/PTO/IR)

### Description

This C++ code compiles and runs fine:

<details>
<summary><code>repro_manual_acc_to_mat.cpp</code> (click to expand)</summary>

```cpp
#define MEMORY_BASE
#include <pto/pto-inst.hpp>

using namespace pto;

extern "C" __global__ AICORE void repro_manual_acc_to_mat(
    __gm__ float *out_ptr, __gm__ half *in_ptr, int32_t n_i32) {
#if (__CHECK_FEATURE_AT_PRECOMPILE) || \
    (__CCE_AICORE__ == 220 && defined(__DAV_C220_CUBE__))
  const uint32_t n = static_cast<uint32_t>(n_i32);

  using TensorShapeIn = TileShape2D<half, 128, 128, Layout::ND>;
  using TensorStridesIn = BaseShape2D<half, 128, 128, Layout::ND>;
  using TensorShapeOut = TileShape2D<float, 128, 128, Layout::ND>;
  using TensorStridesOut = BaseShape2D<float, 128, 128, Layout::ND>;

  using GlobalTensorIn =
      GlobalTensor<half, TensorShapeIn, TensorStridesIn, Layout::ND>;
  using GlobalTensorOut =
      GlobalTensor<float, TensorShapeOut, TensorStridesOut, Layout::ND>;

  using TileL1 = Tile<TileType::Mat, half, 128, 128, BLayout::ColMajor, 128,
                      128, SLayout::RowMajor, 512>;
  using TileL0A = TileLeft<half, 128, 128>;
  using TileL0B = TileRight<half, 128, 128>;
  using TileL0C = TileAcc<float, 128, 128>;

  GlobalTensorIn in_gm(in_ptr);
  GlobalTensorOut out_gm(out_ptr);

  TileL1 y_l1;
  TileL0A a_l0;
  TileL0B b_l0;
  TileL0C c_l0;

  TASSIGN(y_l1, 0x0);
  TASSIGN(a_l0, 0x0);
  TASSIGN(b_l0, 0x0);
  TASSIGN(c_l0, 0x0);

  y_l1.SetValidRow(n);
  y_l1.SetValidCol(n);
  a_l0.SetValidRow(n);
  a_l0.SetValidCol(n);
  b_l0.SetValidRow(n);
  b_l0.SetValidCol(n);
  c_l0.SetValidRow(n);
  c_l0.SetValidCol(n);

  TLOAD(y_l1, in_gm);
  set_flag(PIPE_MTE2, PIPE_MTE1, EVENT_ID0);
  wait_flag(PIPE_MTE2, PIPE_MTE1, EVENT_ID0);

  TMOV(a_l0, y_l1);
  TMOV(b_l0, y_l1);
  set_flag(PIPE_MTE1, PIPE_M, EVENT_ID0);
  wait_flag(PIPE_MTE1, PIPE_M, EVENT_ID0);

  TMATMUL(c_l0, a_l0, b_l0);
  set_flag(PIPE_M, PIPE_FIX, EVENT_ID0);
  wait_flag(PIPE_M, PIPE_FIX, EVENT_ID0);

  TMOV(y_l1, c_l0);  // ACC(float) -> MAT(half): known manual working path
  set_flag(PIPE_FIX, PIPE_M, EVENT_ID0);
  wait_flag(PIPE_FIX, PIPE_M, EVENT_ID0);

  TMATMUL(c_l0, a_l0, b_l0);
  set_flag(PIPE_M, PIPE_FIX, EVENT_ID1);
  wait_flag(PIPE_M, PIPE_FIX, EVENT_ID1);
  TSTORE(out_gm, c_l0);
#endif
}
```

</details>

Notice this line -- TMOV does fp32->fp16 quant on the fly.

```cpp
  TMOV(y_l1, c_l0);  // ACC(float) -> MAT(half): known manual working path
```

Compiles fine by:
```bash
bisheng -fPIC -shared -xcce -O2 -std=c++17 \
  --npu-arch=dav-2201 -DMEMORY_BASE \
  -I"${ASCEND_TOOLKIT_HOME}/include" \
  ./repro_manual_acc_to_mat.cpp \
  -o ./repro_manual_acc_to_mat.so
```

A full working C++ example using this pattern is at https://github.com/huawei-csl/pto-kernels/issues/53

However the ptoas python binding of the same code logic fails with error:

```
error: unknown: 'pto.tmov' op expects src/dst to have the same element type
```


### Reproduction (minimal)

Run this script `python ./reproducer_raw_api.py` you'll see the error.

<details>
<summary><code>reproducer_raw_api.py</code> (click to expand)</summary>

```python
from mlir.dialects import arith, func, pto as _pto
from mlir.ir import (
    Context,
    F16Type,
    F32Type,
    IndexType,
    InsertionPoint,
    IntegerType,
    Location,
    Module,
)


def _idx_const(v: int):
    return arith.ConstantOp(IndexType.get(), v).result


def build_raw_module():
    with Context() as ctx, Location.unknown():
        _pto.register_dialect(ctx, load=True)
        module = Module.create()

        in_dtype = F16Type.get()
        out_dtype = F32Type.get()
        i32 = IntegerType.get_signless(32)

        ptr_in = _pto.PtrType.get(in_dtype)
        ptr_out = _pto.PtrType.get(out_dtype)

        tv_in_ty = _pto.TensorViewType.get(2, in_dtype)
        tv_out_ty = _pto.TensorViewType.get(2, out_dtype)
        st_in_ty = _pto.PartitionTensorViewType.get([128, 128], in_dtype)
        st_out_ty = _pto.PartitionTensorViewType.get([128, 128], out_dtype)

        mat = _pto.AddressSpaceAttr.get(_pto.AddressSpace.MAT)
        left = _pto.AddressSpaceAttr.get(_pto.AddressSpace.LEFT)
        right = _pto.AddressSpaceAttr.get(_pto.AddressSpace.RIGHT)
        acc = _pto.AddressSpaceAttr.get(_pto.AddressSpace.ACC)

        cfg_mat = _pto.TileBufConfigAttr.get(
            _pto.BLayoutAttr.get(_pto.BLayout.ColMajor),
            _pto.SLayoutAttr.get(_pto.SLayout.RowMajor),
            _pto.TileConfig.fractalABSize,
            _pto.PadValueAttr.get(_pto.PadValue.Null),
        )
        cfg_left = _pto.TileBufConfigAttr.get(
            _pto.BLayoutAttr.get(_pto.BLayout.RowMajor),
            _pto.SLayoutAttr.get(_pto.SLayout.RowMajor),
            _pto.TileConfig.fractalABSize,
            _pto.PadValueAttr.get(_pto.PadValue.Null),
        )
        cfg_right = _pto.TileBufConfigAttr.get(
            _pto.BLayoutAttr.get(_pto.BLayout.RowMajor),
            _pto.SLayoutAttr.get(_pto.SLayout.ColMajor),
            _pto.TileConfig.fractalABSize,
            _pto.PadValueAttr.get(_pto.PadValue.Null),
        )
        cfg_acc = _pto.TileBufConfigAttr.get(
            _pto.BLayoutAttr.get(_pto.BLayout.ColMajor),
            _pto.SLayoutAttr.get(_pto.SLayout.RowMajor),
            _pto.TileConfig.fractalCSize,
            _pto.PadValueAttr.get(_pto.PadValue.Null),
        )

        tile_mat = _pto.TileBufType.get([128, 128], in_dtype, mat, [-1, -1], cfg_mat)
        tile_left = _pto.TileBufType.get(
            [128, 128], in_dtype, left, [-1, -1], cfg_left
        )
        tile_right = _pto.TileBufType.get(
            [128, 128], in_dtype, right, [-1, -1], cfg_right
        )
        tile_acc = _pto.TileBufType.get([128, 128], out_dtype, acc, [-1, -1], cfg_acc)

        fn_ty = func.FunctionType.get([ptr_out, ptr_in, i32], [])
        with InsertionPoint(module.body):
            fn = func.FuncOp("reproducer_raw_api", fn_ty)
            entry = fn.add_entry_block()

        with InsertionPoint(entry):
            out_ptr, in_ptr, n_i32 = entry.arguments
            n = arith.IndexCastOp(IndexType.get(), n_i32).result
            c0 = _idx_const(0)
            c1 = _idx_const(1)

            cube = _pto.SectionCubeOp()
            cube_block = cube.body.blocks.append()
            with InsertionPoint(cube_block):
                tv_in = _pto.MakeTensorViewOp(tv_in_ty, in_ptr, [n, n], [n, c1]).result
                tv_out = _pto.MakeTensorViewOp(
                    tv_out_ty, out_ptr, [n, n], [n, c1]
                ).result

                sv_in = _pto.PartitionViewOp(
                    st_in_ty, tv_in, offsets=[c0, c0], sizes=[n, n]
                ).result
                sv_out = _pto.PartitionViewOp(
                    st_out_ty, tv_out, offsets=[c0, c0], sizes=[n, n]
                ).result

                tmat = _pto.AllocTileOp(tile_mat, valid_row=n, valid_col=n).result
                ta = _pto.AllocTileOp(tile_left, valid_row=n, valid_col=n).result
                tb = _pto.AllocTileOp(tile_right, valid_row=n, valid_col=n).result
                tc = _pto.AllocTileOp(tile_acc, valid_row=n, valid_col=n).result

                _pto.TLoadOp(None, sv_in, tmat)
                _pto.TMovOp(None, tmat, ta)
                _pto.TMovOp(None, tmat, tb)
                _pto.TMatmulOp(None, ta, tb, tc)
                _pto.TMovOp(None, tc, tmat)  # ACC -> MAT: expected failure
                _pto.TStoreOp(None, tc, sv_out)

            func.ReturnOp([])

        module.operation.verify()
        return module


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(build_raw_module())
```

    %wq_chunk_0_tile = pto.alloc_tile : !pto.tile_buf<loc=mat, dtype=bf16, rows=256, cols=64, v_row=256, v_col=64, blayout=col_major, slayout=row_major, fractal=512, pad=0>
    %wq_chunk_0_tile_Right = pto.alloc_tile : !pto.tile_buf<loc=right, dtype=bf16, rows=256, cols=64, v_row=256, v_col=64, blayout=row_major, slayout=col_major, fractal=512, pad=0>
    %_t6_tile_Left = pto.alloc_tile : !pto.tile_buf<loc=left, dtype=bf16, rows=4, cols=256, v_row=4, v_col=256, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>
    %_t7_tile = pto.alloc_tile : !pto.tile_buf<loc=acc, dtype=f32, rows=4, cols=64, v_row=4, v_col=64, blayout=col_major, slayout=row_major, fractal=1024, pad=0>
    scf.for %ob_0_in = %c0 to %c4 step %c1 {
      %0 = arith.muli %arg4, %c4 : index
      %1 = arith.addi %0, %ob_0_in : index
      %2 = arith.muli %1, %c1 : index
      %3 = arith.addi %c0, %2 : index
      %4 = arith.muli %3, %c64 : index
      scf.for %kb_1 = %c0 to %c20 step %c1 {
        %5 = arith.muli %kb_1, %c256 : index
        %wq_0_pview = pto.partition_view %wq_0_view, offsets = [%5, %4], sizes = [%c256, %c64] : !pto.tensor_view<?x?xbf16> -> !pto.partition_tensor_view<256x64xbf16>
        pto.tload ins(%wq_0_pview : !pto.partition_tensor_view<256x64xbf16>) outs(%wq_chunk_0_tile : !pto.tile_buf<loc=mat, dtype=bf16, rows=256, cols=64, v_row=256, v_col=64, blayout=col_major, slayout=row_major, fractal=512, pad=0>)
        pto.tmov ins(%wq_chunk_0_tile : !pto.tile_buf<loc=mat, dtype=bf16, rows=256, cols=64, v_row=256, v_col=64, blayout=col_major, slayout=row_major, fractal=512, pad=0>) outs(%wq_chunk_0_tile_Right : !pto.tile_buf<loc=right, dtype=bf16, rows=256, cols=64, v_row=256, v_col=64, blayout=row_major, slayout=col_major, fractal=512, pad=0>)
        pto.tpop_from_aiv outs(%_t6_tile_Left : !pto.tile_buf<loc=left, dtype=bf16, rows=4, cols=256, v_row=4, v_col=256, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>) {aiv_idx = 0}
        pto.tmatmul ins(%_t6_tile_Left, %wq_chunk_0_tile_Right : !pto.tile_buf<loc=left, dtype=bf16, rows=4, cols=256, v_row=4, v_col=256, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>, !pto.tile_buf<loc=right, dtype=bf16, rows=256, cols=64, v_row=256, v_col=64, blayout=row_major, slayout=col_major, fractal=512, pad=0>) outs(%_t7_tile : !pto.tile_buf<loc=acc, dtype=f32, rows=4, cols=64, v_row=4, v_col=64, blayout=col_major, slayout=row_major, fractal=1024, pad=0>)
        pto.tpush_to_aiv ins(%_t7_tile : !pto.tile_buf<loc=acc, dtype=f32, rows=4, cols=64, v_row=4, v_col=64, blayout=col_major, slayout=row_major, fractal=1024, pad=0>) {aiv_idx = 0}
      }
    }
    return
  }
}

For an IR containing `pto.tmov` from `acc` to `mat` (L0C to L1), `ptoas --enable-insert-sync` does not insert enough sync around `TMOV`, leading to error during kernel execution: `errorStr: L0C read/write conflict(vec read operation or cube write operation).When the FIXP reads l0c, the read and write operations occur at the same address.`

## #305 npu_validation run.sh template redundantly reruns golden.py and NPU executable in GOLDEN_MODE=npu

- State: closed
- URL: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/PTOAS/issues/305
- Created: 2026-03-19T01:50:23Z
- Updated: 2026-04-01T01:26:18Z
- Closed: 2026-04-01T01:26:18Z

### Body

## Summary
`test/npu_validation/templates/run_sh_template.sh` currently performs redundant work in `GOLDEN_MODE=npu`:
- `golden.py` is executed twice
- the NPU executable is also executed twice

This makes each NPU validation case slower than necessary and increases overall validation time.

## Affected code
File: `test/npu_validation/templates/run_sh_template.sh`

Current `npu)` branch:
```bash
python3 "${ROOT_DIR}/golden.py"
LD_LIBRARY_PATH="${LD_LIBRARY_PATH_NPU}" "${ROOT_DIR}/${BUILD_DIR}/@EXECUTABLE@"
copy_outputs_as_golden
python3 "${ROOT_DIR}/golden.py"
LD_LIBRARY_PATH="${LD_LIBRARY_PATH_NPU}" "${ROOT_DIR}/${BUILD_DIR}/@EXECUTABLE@"
COMPARE_STRICT=1 python3 "${ROOT_DIR}/compare.py"
```

## Problem
For the `npu)` branch, the final comparison only needs:
1. one Python golden generation
2. one NPU execution
3. one compare step

The current flow does more work than needed:
- first `golden.py`
- first NPU run
- `copy_outputs_as_golden`
- second `golden.py`
- second NPU run
- compare

So every case pays for an extra Python golden generation and an extra NPU execution.

## Impact
This increases test latency for every generated NPU validation case.
When running many cases in batch, the redundant execution can significantly increase total validation time.

It also makes the control flow harder to understand because `copy_outputs_as_golden` is not needed if the script is going to regenerate the Python golden again before the final compare.

## Expected behavior
In `GOLDEN_MODE=npu`, the script should:
1. generate Python golden once with `golden.py`
2. run the NPU executable once
3. compare NPU output against the golden

## Suggested fix
Simplify the `npu)` branch to:
```bash
python3 "${ROOT_DIR}/golden.py"
LD_LIBRARY_PATH="${LD_LIBRARY_PATH_NPU}" "${ROOT_DIR}/${BUILD_DIR}/@EXECUTABLE@"
COMPARE_STRICT=1 python3 "${ROOT_DIR}/compare.py"
```

and remove the redundant:
- extra `golden.py`
- extra NPU run
- `copy_outputs_as_golden` call in the `npu)` branch

## #321 CSE incorrectly eliminates treshape on mutated tile_buf

- State: closed
- URL: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/PTOAS/issues/321
- Created: 2026-03-20T03:39:11Z
- Updated: 2026-03-24T02:05:14Z
- Closed: 2026-03-24T02:05:13Z

### Body

## Summary

`ptoas` CSE (Common Subexpression Elimination) incorrectly merges two `pto.treshape` operations that reference the same `tile_buf` when the buffer is mutated by an intervening `pto.trowsum` write.

## Reproduction

**Input MLIR (`.pto`)** — two `treshape %t__tile` separated by a `trowsum` that overwrites `%t__tile`:

```mlir
    // 1st row_sum: writes sum(x) into %t__tile
    pto.trowsum ins(%tile_x__tile, %tmp_tile : ...) outs(%t__tile : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, rows=32, cols=1, ...blayout=col_major...>)

    // 1st reshape: reads %t__tile (contains sum(x))
    %reshape_buf = pto.treshape %t__tile : !pto.tile_buf<...rows=32, cols=1...blayout=col_major...> -> !pto.tile_buf<...rows=1, cols=32...blayout=row_major...>

    // consume %reshape_buf
    pto.tmuls ins(%reshape_buf, %cst : ..., f32) outs(%mean_T__tile : ...)

    // ... intervening ops ...

    // 2nd row_sum: OVERWRITES %t__tile with sum(centred²)
    pto.trowsum ins(%0, %1 : ...) outs(%t__tile : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, rows=32, cols=1, ...blayout=col_major...>)

    // 2nd reshape: should read UPDATED %t__tile (contains sum(centred²))
    %7 = pto.treshape %t__tile : !pto.tile_buf<...rows=32, cols=1...blayout=col_major...> -> !pto.tile_buf<...rows=1, cols=32...blayout=row_major...>

    // consume %7
    pto.tmuls ins(%7, %cst : ..., f32) outs(%mean_T__tile : ...)
```

**Expected C++ output** — two separate `TRESHAPE` calls:

```cpp
TROWSUM(v32, v28, v31);       // 1st row_sum → v32
TRESHAPE(v47, v32);            // 1st reshape: v47 = reshape(v32), reads sum(x)
TMULS(v33, v47, v13);          // mean = sum(x) / N
// ...
TROWSUM(v32, v34, v35);       // 2nd row_sum → v32 (overwritten!)
TRESHAPE(v47, v32);            // 2nd reshape: v47 = reshape(v32), reads sum(centred²)  ← EXPECTED
TMULS(v33, v47, v13);          // var = sum(centred²) / N
```

**Actual C++ output** — second `TRESHAPE` is eliminated:

```cpp
TROWSUM(v32, v28, v31);       // 1st row_sum → v32
TRESHAPE(v47, v32);            // 1st reshape
TMULS(v33, v47, v13);          // mean = sum(x) / N  ✓
// ...
TROWSUM(v32, v34, v35);       // 2nd row_sum → v32 (overwritten!)
                                // ← MISSING: TRESHAPE(v47, v32)
TMULS(v33, v47, v13);          // WRONG: reads stale v47 = sum(x)/N instead of sum(centred²)/N
```

## Impact

The kernel computes `inv_std = rsqrt(mean + eps)` instead of `rsqrt(variance + eps)`, causing ~93% of output elements to be incorrect. Verified on simulator.

## Root Cause

`pto.treshape` reads from a mutable `tile_buf`. The CSE pass treats two `treshape` ops with the same source SSA name and type as identical, but does not check for intervening writes (`pto.trowsum ... outs(...)`) that mutate the source buffer between the two reads. The two `treshape` ops actually read different data and must not be merged.

## Suggested Fix

`pto.treshape` should declare a **Read** memory effect on its source operand. CSE should then verify no intervening **Write** effect exists on the same buffer before merging.

## Attachments

Full `.pto` and `.cpp` files attached below.

[layer_norm_incore_0.pto.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26131979/layer_norm_incore_0.pto.txt)

[layer_norm_incore_0.cpp](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26131976/layer_norm_incore_0.cpp)

## #322 TStore verifier should reject tile/partition shape mismatch and subset should not allow enlarging tile shape

- State: closed
- URL: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/PTOAS/issues/322
- Created: 2026-03-20T03:40:44Z
- Updated: 2026-04-23T07:39:43Z
- Closed: 2026-04-23T07:39:43Z

### Body

## Summary

`pto.tstore` currently accepts IR where the destination partition shape is larger than the source tile valid shape.

This later lowers to PTO-ISA C++ like:

```cpp
GlobalTensor<float, ..., Shape<..., 64, 64>, ...> dst = ...;
Tile<..., 64, 64, ..., 32, 32, ...> tile = ...;
TSTORE(dst, tile);
```

For PTO-ISA there is an implicit constraint: during `TSTORE`, the `GlobalTensor` shape must match the tile valid shape. The current verifier does not enforce this, so invalid IR can pass verification and only show up much later in generated code.

## Reproducer

A generated case from this repo already demonstrates the problem:

- source test case:
  `test/pto_isa_st/TMaxs/tmaxs_float_64x64_32x32_32x32.py`
- generated PTO IR:
  `build/output/TMaxs/tmaxs_float_64x64_32x32_32x32-pto-ir.pto`
- generated kernel:
  `build/output_npu_validation/TMaxs/tmaxs_float_64x64_32x32_32x32/tmaxs_float_64x64_32x32_32x32_kernel.cpp`

Relevant PTO IR:

```mlir
%4 = pto.alloc_tile : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, rows=32, cols=32, v_row=32, v_col=32, ...>
%5 = pto.alloc_tile : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, rows=64, cols=64, v_row=32, v_col=32, ...>
%7 = pto.subset %4[%c0_5, %c0_5] sizes [64, 64] : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, rows=32, cols=32, v_row=32, v_col=32, ...>
pto.tmaxs ins(%7, %6 : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, rows=64, cols=64, v_row=32, v_col=32, ...>, f32)
  outs(%5 : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, rows=64, cols=64, v_row=32, v_col=32, ...>)
pto.tstore ins(%5 : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, rows=64, cols=64, v_row=32, v_col=32, ...>)
  outs(%3 : !pto.partition_tensor_view<64x64xf32>)
```

This verifies today, but should be rejected earlier.

## Root cause

There seem to be two gaps:

1. `TStoreOp::verify()` checks element types / address spaces, but does not check that destination partition shape matches the source tile valid shape.
2. `SubsetOp::verify()` does not reject non-boxed subsets that enlarge the tile shape, so a `32x32` tile can become a `subset ... sizes [64, 64]`.

Because of that, invalid IR is accepted and codegen simply materializes the mismatch.

## Expected behavior

At least one of the following should be enforced:

1. `pto.tstore` verifier should reject cases where:
   - dst partition rank/shape does not match src tile valid shape
   - especially for static cases, `dst shape != src valid_shape`
2. `pto.subset` verifier should reject shape enlargement:
   - subset result sizes must not exceed source tile shape
   - ideally also remain consistent with valid-shape semantics

## Why this matters

Without this check, invalid test cases or frontend bugs can silently generate PTO IR that looks structurally valid but violates PTO-ISA constraints at `TSTORE` lowering time.

## Suggested fix

- Add a shape compatibility check in `TStoreOp::verify()`
- Add a no-enlargement check in `SubsetOp::verify()`
- Optionally add a regression test using the existing `tmaxs_float_64x64_32x32_32x32` pattern

## Local reference points

- `lib/PTO/IR/PTO.cpp`:
  - `TStoreOp::verify()`
  - `SubsetOp::verify()`
- `test/sample_utils/pto_isa_st_cases.py`:
  - `_subset_if_needed()` currently builds `pto.subset(... sizes=[dst_shape])` whenever `src_shape != dst_shape`, even when `dst_shape > src_shape`

## #326 [Docs] pto.tsort32 and pto.tmrgsort are incorrectly documented in PTO_IR_manual.md

- State: closed
- URL: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/PTOAS/issues/326
- Created: 2026-03-23T01:25:01Z
- Updated: 2026-03-27T03:21:40Z
- Closed: 2026-03-27T03:21:40Z

### Body

### Documentation location

`docs/PTO_IR_manual.md`, Section 4.11 Sorting Operations:
- `pto.tsort32` (Sort Fixed 32-Element Blocks)
- `pto.tmrgsort` (Merge Sort)

### What's wrong or missing?

Two related errors in the sort operation documentation:

#### 1. `pto.tsort32` — output format is interleaved, not two separate buffers

The manual documents `pto.tsort32` as writing two separate output buffers:

| Name | Type | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `dst` | `pto.tile_buf` | Sorted output |
| `idx` | `pto.tile_buf` | Index mapping output |

And the assembly format:

```mlir
pto.tsort32 ins(%src : !pto.tile_buf<...>)
           outs(%dst, %idx : !pto.tile_buf<...>, !pto.tile_buf<...>)
```

**Actual hardware behavior:** `pto.tsort32` writes a single **interleaved** buffer into `dst` of size `2N`:

```
dst = [val_0, idx_0, val_1, idx_1, ..., val_{N-1}, idx_{N-1}]
```

Where:
- `val_i` is the i-th sorted element value (`f16` or `f32`)
- `idx_i` is the permutation index stored as the same float type (`f16`/`f32`)
- Elements are in **descending** order (`val_0 ≥ val_1 ≥ ... ≥ val_{N-1}`)

So:
- `dst` has shape `[rows, 2N]` (twice the input width), not `[rows, N]`
- The `idx` output operand described in the manual is **not populated** — the hardware writes everything into `dst` in interleaved form

**Evidence:** Runtime execution of a 1×32 sort yields `dst = [2.397, 28.0, 1.465, 22.0, ...]` (values and indices alternating) rather than `dst = [2.397, 1.465, ...]` + a separate `idx = [28, 22, ...]`.

#### 2. `pto.tmrgsort` — `blockLen` is an SSA operand, not a keyword attribute

The manual shows:

```mlir
pto.tmrgsort ins(%src : !pto.tile_buf<...>) outs(%dst : !pto.tile_buf<...>) blockLen = 32
```

And describes `blockLen` as `I32Attr`.

**Actual assembly format:**

```mlir
%mrgsort_blen_64 = arith.constant 64 : i32
pto.tmrgsort ins(%src, %mrgsort_blen_64 : !pto.tile_buf<...>, i32)
            outs(%dst : !pto.tile_buf<...>)
```

`blockLen` is an **SSA value** passed as the second operand in `ins()`, not a keyword attribute.

Additionally, the physical `blockLen` passed to the hardware must be **twice** the logical block length, because the hardware counts interleaved `(value, index)` pairs — i.e., a logical block of 32 elements corresponds to a physical `blockLen = 64`.

The manual's constraint `blockLen must be a multiple of 64` is correct for the physical value, but the manual does not explain that the physical value is 2× the logical element count.

### Suggested improvement

For **`pto.tsort32`**:

1. Update the output description to show a single `dst` of width `2N` in interleaved format
2. Remove or clarify the `idx` output operand (it is not written by the hardware)
3. Add a data layout diagram showing the interleaved `[val, idx, val, idx, ...]` format
4. Clarify that element type of the index values is the same as the value type (`f16`/`f32`), not `u32`

For **`pto.tmrgsort`**:

1. Update the assembly format to show `blockLen` as an SSA operand in `ins()`
2. Clarify that `blockLen` is the physical count of interleaved pairs (= 2 × logical element count)
3. Update the argument table: change `I32Attr` to `i32 SSA value`
4. Add a note that input `src` must be in the interleaved format produced by `pto.tsort32`

## #328 [Bug] PTOAS MLIR Parsing Error: `tpush_to_aiv` and `tpush_to_aic` Syntax Mismatch

- State: closed
- URL: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/PTOAS/issues/328
- Created: 2026-03-23T02:41:00Z
- Updated: 2026-03-26T07:05:00Z
- Closed: 2026-03-26T07:05:00Z

### Body

### Component

PTO Dialect / ODS (include/PTO/IR)

### Description

# PTOAS MLIR 解析错误：`tpush_to_aiv` 和 `tpush_to_aic` 语法不匹配

## 运行环境

- **工作目录**: `/data/x00952168/pypto3.0`
- **pypto Commit ID**: `2374445` (refactor(ir): remove OpStmts IR node (#663))
- **PTOAS Commit ID**: `08187e0` (Merge pull request #312 from TaoTao-real/codex/set-wait-unified-api-clean)
- **pypto-lib Commit ID**: `7c6afa7` (Add layer_norm example and auto-discover examples in CI (#29))
- **PTOAS 版本**: 0.12

## 启动命令

```bash
cd /data/x00952168/pypto3.0/pypto-lib/examples/qwen3
python qwen3_32b_prefill.py
```

## 输出路径

- **构建输出目录**: `/data/x00952168/build_output/Qwen3SingleLayerPrefill_20260323_094832/`
- **错误报告**: `/data/x00952168/build_output/Qwen3SingleLayerPrefill_20260323_094832/report/codegen_errors.txt`
- **生成的 PTO 文件**: `/data/x00952168/build_output/Qwen3SingleLayerPrefill_20260323_094832/ptoas/*.pto`

## 问题定位

### 错误信息
```
Failed to compile function 'qwen3_prefill_layer_incore_10_aic': ptoas compilation failed: 
loc("build_output/.../qwen3_prefill_layer_incore_10_aic.pto":37:21): error: expected '('
```

### 具体文件和行号
**文件**: `qwen3_prefill_layer_incore_10_aic.pto` (第37行)

**pypto 生成的代码**:
```mlir
pto.tpush_to_aiv ins(%t__tile : !pto.tile_buf<loc=acc, dtype=f32, rows=4, cols=64, ...>) {aiv_idx = 0}
```

**问题位置截图**:
```
第36行: pto.tmatmul ins(...) outs(...)
第37行: pto.tpush_to_aiv ins(%t__tile : !pto.tile_buf<...>) {aiv_idx = 0}
              ^
              错误: 在位置21处期望'('
```

### 受影响的函数（共11个）
所有函数都因类似语法错误而失败：
- `qwen3_prefill_layer_incore_10_aic` / `qwen3_prefill_layer_incore_10_aiv`
- `qwen3_prefill_layer_incore_1_aic` / `qwen3_prefill_layer_incore_1_aiv`
- `qwen3_prefill_layer_incore_2_aic` / `qwen3_prefill_layer_incore_2_aiv`
- `qwen3_prefill_layer_incore_5_aic`
- `qwen3_prefill_layer_incore_6_aic` / `qwen3_prefill_layer_incore_6_aiv`
- `qwen3_prefill_layer_incore_9_aic` / `qwen3_prefill_layer_incore_9_aiv`

## 根因分析

### pypto 与 PTOAS 之间的语法不匹配

**PTOAS 期望的语法**（来自 `PTOAS/include/PTO/IR/PTOOps.td` 第1244-1247行）：
```mlir
pto.tpush_to_aiv(%tile : qualified(type($tile))) {split = $split}
```

**pypto 实际生成的语法**:
```mlir
pto.tpush_to_aiv ins(%tile : type) {aiv_idx = 0}
```

### 关键差异点：

1. **输入格式**: 
   - PTOAS 期望: `(%tile : type)` - 直接使用括号
   - pypto 生成: `ins(%tile : type)` - 使用 `ins` 关键字

2. **属性名称**:
   - PTOAS 期望: `{split = value}`
   - pypto 生成: `{aiv_idx = 0}`

3. **操作变体**:
   - `tpush_to_aiv` 期望 `split` 属性
   - `tpush_to_aic` 期望 `split` 属性
   - pypto 生成 `aiv_idx` / `aic_idx` 属性


### Reproduction (minimal)

```markdown
// test_tpush_syntax.pto
module {
  func.func @test_tpush(%tile: !pto.tile_buf<loc=acc, dtype=f32, rows=4, cols=64, v_row=4, v_col=64, blayout=col_major, slayout=row_major, fractal=1024, pad=0>) {
    // 这行会导致解析错误
    pto.tpush_to_aiv ins(%tile : !pto.tile_buf<loc=acc, dtype=f32, rows=4, cols=64, v_row=4, v_col=64, blayout=col_major, slayout=row_major, fractal=1024, pad=0>) {aiv_idx = 0}
    return
  }
}
```

### Expected behavior

正常完成解析。

### Actual behavior / error logs

```text
见描述
```

v0.12

Linux (aarch64)

None

### PTOAS build level (if relevant)

## #331 [Feature] Improve !pto.tile_buf IR readability by eliding default fields and supporting aliases

- State: closed
- URL: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/PTOAS/issues/331
- Created: 2026-03-23T03:33:20Z
- Updated: 2026-04-09T09:49:04Z
- Closed: 2026-04-09T09:49:04Z

### Body

## Problem

The current custom assembly printer for `!pto.tile_buf` always prints the full parameter list:

- `loc`
- `dtype`
- `rows`
- `cols`
- `v_row`
- `v_col`
- `blayout`
- `slayout`
- `fractal`
- `pad`

This makes PTO IR very hard to read in fusion-heavy regions, because the same long type string is repeated on nearly every operand/result.

The current behavior comes from the custom parser/printer in `lib/PTO/IR/PTOTypeDefs.cpp`:

- `TileBufType::parse`: currently expects the full keyed form in a fixed order
- `TileBufType::print`: currently always emits the full keyed form

## Example

From a real IR dump in this checkout:

```mlir
pto.tmax ins(%arg9, %arg10 : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, rows=1, cols=16, v_row=1, v_col=16, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>, !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, rows=1, cols=16, v_row=1, v_col=16, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>) outs(%arg11 : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, rows=1, cols=16, v_row=1, v_col=16, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>)
pto.tsub ins(%arg9, %arg11 : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, rows=1, cols=16, v_row=1, v_col=16, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>, !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, rows=1, cols=16, v_row=1, v_col=16, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>) outs(%arg12 : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, rows=1, cols=16, v_row=1, v_col=16, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>)
```

When this appears inside `pto.fusion_region`, block arguments, yields, and function-like signatures all become visually dominated by repeated type text rather than the actual dataflow.

## Why this matters

This is mainly a readability and debugging problem:

- reviewing fusion/grouping/scheduling output is slower than necessary
- IR diffs become noisy
- region signatures and `pto.yield` lines become much harder to scan
- repeated default config values hide the semantically important differences

## Suggested direction

I suggest keeping the current verbose syntax parseable for backward compatibility, but changing the default printer to a more compact form.

### 1. Elide redundant/default fields in the default printer

Possible rules:

- omit `v_row` / `v_col` when they are equal to `rows` / `cols`
- omit config fields when the config is the dialect default
  - `blayout=row_major`
  - `slayout=none_box`
  - `fractal=512`
  - `pad=0`
- compress `rows + cols + dtype` into a shaped form such as `1x16xf32`

For example:

Current:

```mlir
!pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, rows=1, cols=16, v_row=1, v_col=16, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>
```

Possible compact default:

```mlir
!pto.tile_buf<vec, 1x16xf32>
```

And when valid shape / layout differ from defaults:

```mlir
!pto.tile_buf<vec, 16x128xf32, valid=16x1, blayout=col_major>
```

### 2. Support type aliases for repeated tile_buf instances

For very repetitive IR, consider adding an `OpAsmDialectInterface` alias path so repeated identical tile types can print once and then be referenced via a short alias.

For example:

```mlir
!pto.tb0 = !pto.tile_buf<vec, 1x16xf32>
```

Then ops can use `!pto.tb0` instead of repeating the full type.

### 3. Keep a verbose/debug path available

If full information is still useful for debugging, we can keep either:

- the current syntax accepted by the parser
- an explicit verbose printing mode / debug flag

That way we improve default readability without losing inspectability.

## Expected outcome

- shorter and more readable IR dumps
- much cleaner fusion-region and block-argument printing
- lower diff noise
- no semantic change to `tile_buf`
- backward-compatible parser behavior

## Scope

This request is only about assembly syntax / textual readability. It does **not** request any change to tile semantics, layout semantics, or type invariants.


---

## #345 Bug: ptoas converts Left tile blayout from col_major to row_major

- State: closed
- URL: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/PTOAS/issues/345
- Created: 2026-03-24T11:22:44Z
- Updated: 2026-03-26T07:03:55Z
- Closed: 2026-03-26T07:03:55Z

### Body

## Summary

When ptoas processes a `.pto` file containing `loc=left` tiles with `blayout=col_major`, the output C++ code incorrectly emits `BLayout::RowMajor` instead of `BLayout::ColMajor`. This causes incorrect matrix multiplication results.

## Reproduction

**Input PTO IR** — Left tiles declared with `blayout=col_major`:

```mlir
%tile_a__tile_Left = pto.alloc_tile addr = %c0i : !pto.tile_buf<loc=left, dtype=f16, rows=64, cols=64, v_row=64, v_col=64, blayout=col_major, slayout=row_major, fractal=512, pad=0>
pto.tmov ins(%tile_a__tile : !pto.tile_buf<loc=mat, ..., blayout=col_major, ...>) outs(%tile_a__tile_Left : !pto.tile_buf<loc=left, ..., blayout=col_major, ...>)
```

**ptoas command:**

```bash
ptoas gemm_incore_0.pto -o gemm_incore_0.cpp --enable-insert-sync --pto-level=level3
```

**Actual output C++** — Left tile BLayout is RowMajor (wrong):

```cpp
// line 60
Tile<TileType::Left, half, 64, 64, BLayout::RowMajor, 64, 64, SLayout::RowMajor, 512, PadValue::Null> v28;
// line 99
Tile<TileType::Left, half, 64, 64, BLayout::RowMajor, 64, 64, SLayout::RowMajor, 512, PadValue::Null> v42;
```

**Expected output C++** — Left tile BLayout should be ColMajor:

```cpp
Tile<TileType::Left, half, 64, 64, BLayout::ColMajor, 64, 64, SLayout::RowMajor, 512, PadValue::Null> v28;
Tile<TileType::Left, half, 64, 64, BLayout::ColMajor, 64, 64, SLayout::RowMajor, 512, PadValue::Null> v42;
```

## Root Cause

In the ptoas internal IR, `pto.pointer_cast` for `address_space<left>` tiles shows `blayout=#pto.blayout<row_major>`, even though the input `pto.alloc_tile` specifies `blayout=col_major`:

```mlir
// ptoas intermediate (wrong — col_major was overwritten to row_major):
%7 = pto.pointer_cast(%c0_i64) ... {config = #pto.tile_buf_config<blayout=#pto.blayout<row_major>, ...>}
    : memref<64x64xf16, strided<[64, 16], offset: ?>, #pto.address_space<left>>
```

It appears ptoas forcibly overrides `blayout` based on `address_space` rather than preserving the value from the input IR.

## Impact

Manually patching the generated C++ from `RowMajor` to `ColMajor` for Left tiles produces correct GEMM results. Without the fix, matrix multiplication outputs are entirely wrong (65531/65536 elements mismatched).

## Other Tile Types (for reference)

| TileType | blayout in PTO IR | blayout in C++ output | Correct? |
|----------|------------------|-----------------------|----------|
| Mat      | col_major        | ColMajor              | Yes      |
| Left     | col_major        | **RowMajor**          | **No**   |
| Right    | row_major        | RowMajor              | Yes      |
| Acc      | col_major        | ColMajor              | Yes      |

## #358 [Bug] TPUSH/TPOP 模板参数中 Tile 的 BLayout/SLayout 与实际 Tile 声明不一致

- State: closed
- URL: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/PTOAS/issues/358
- Created: 2026-03-25T10:33:46Z
- Updated: 2026-03-25T23:51:29Z
- Closed: 2026-03-25T23:51:29Z

### Body

### Component

EmitC / Codegen (lib/PTO/Transforms/PTOToEmitC.cpp)

### Description

ptoas 在生成 `TPUSH` / `TPOP` 指令的 C++ 模板参数时，**没有使用被 push/pop 的 Tile 变量的实际 layout 信息**，而是错误地使用了默认的 `BLayout::RowMajor, SLayout::NoneBox`。

具体表现：当 PTO IR 中的 tile 具有 `blayout=col_major, slayout=row_major` 时，ptoas 生成的 `TPUSH` / `TPOP` 模板参数中的 Tile 类型却使用了 `BLayout::RowMajor, SLayout::NoneBox`。

该问题在 AIV（vector）侧的 TPUSH 和 TPOP 指令上均可复现。AIC（cube）侧的 TPUSH/TPOP 模板参数是正确的。


### Reproduction (minimal)

```markdown
func.func @scope3_incore_0_incore_0_aiv(...)
{
  ...
  pto.tpush_to_aic(%a_chunk__tile_nz : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=bf16, rows=16, cols=128, v_row=16, v_col=128, layout=col_major, slayout=row_major, fractal=512, pad=0>) {split = 0}
  %t__tile_Vec_nz = pto.tpop_from_aic {split = 0} -> !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, rows=16, cols=64, v_row=16, v_col=64, blayout=col_major, slayout=row_major, fractal=1024, pad=0>
  ...
}
```

### Expected behavior

```cpp
// v44 声明为 BLayout::ColMajor, SLayout::RowMajor（正确）
Tile<TileType::Vec, bfloat16_t, 16, 128, BLayout::ColMajor, 16, 128, SLayout::RowMajor, 512, PadValue::Null> v44;
TASSIGN(v44, v23);
TMOV(v44, v43);

// TPUSH 模板参数应匹配 v44 的类型
TPUSH<TPipe<2, Direction::DIR_V2C, 4096, 4>,
      Tile<TileType::Vec, bfloat16_t, 16, 128, BLayout::ColMajor, 16, 128, SLayout::RowMajor, 512, PadValue::Null>,
      TileSplitAxis::TILE_NO_SPLIT>(v33, v44);
```

```cpp
// TPOP 应使用 ColMajor/RowMajor（与 AIC 侧 TPUSH 的 Tile 类型匹配）
Tile<TileType::Vec, float, 16, 64, BLayout::ColMajor, 16, 64, SLayout::RowMajor, 1024, PadValue::Null> v45;
TPOP<TPipe<0, Direction::DIR_C2V, 4096, 4>,
     Tile<TileType::Vec, float, 16, 64, BLayout::ColMajor, 16, 64, SLayout::RowMajor, 1024, PadValue::Null>,
     TileSplitAxis::TILE_NO_SPLIT>(v32, v45);
```

### Actual behavior / error logs

```text
// v44 声明正确
Tile<TileType::Vec, bfloat16_t, 16, 128, BLayout::ColMajor, 16, 128, SLayout::RowMajor, 512, PadValue::Null> v44;

// ❌ TPUSH 模板参数错误：BLayout::RowMajor, SLayout::NoneBox
TPUSH<TPipe<2, Direction::DIR_V2C, 4096, 4>,
```

## #380 [Bug] First compilation after fresh install always times out

- State: closed
- URL: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/PTOAS/issues/380
- Created: 2026-03-27T09:46:08Z
- Updated: 2026-04-07T02:37:51Z
- Closed: 2026-04-07T02:37:51Z

### Body

### Diagnosis

**ptoas** — After downloading/installing a new ptoas binary, the very first compilation task always times out. Subsequent compilations work normally. This suggests a cold-start overhead issue in ptoas (e.g. lazy initialization, cache warm-up, or dynamic library loading on first run).

### Description

Every time a fresh ptoas binary is downloaded, the first compilation group encounters a 60-second timeout:

```
Failed to compile group 'qwen3_decode_layer_incore_1' [qwen3_decode_layer_incore_1_aic, qwen3_decode_layer_incore_1_aiv]: ptoas compilation timed out after 60s
```

**Steps to reproduce:**

1. Download a fresh ptoas binary from [PTOAS GitHub Releases](https://github.com/zhangstevenunity/PTOAS/releases) (e.g. `ptoas-bin-macos-aarch64.tar.gz`)
2. Extract and set `PTOAS_ROOT` to the extracted directory
3. Run any compilation that invokes ptoas, e.g. `python3 examples/models/qwen3/qwen3_32b_decode_tilelet.py` (from [pypto-lib](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto-lib))
4. The first ptoas compilation group times out after 60s
5. Re-running the same script succeeds without timeout

**Workaround:** Run any trivial compilation first to "warm up" ptoas, then run the actual task.

### Environment

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| ptoas | `v0.17` |
| pypto-lib | `3acde04` |
| pypto | `50a84d7` (branch: `main`) |

### Host Platform

macOS (arm64)

### Additional Context

This issue is reproducible on every fresh ptoas install. The `ptoas --version` check also exhibits similar behavior — it times out on the first invocation (observed with a 20s timeout). This strongly suggests a one-time cold-start cost in the ptoas binary.

## #421 [Assembler] Identity pto.tmov (dst == src) causes spurious sync insertion, hanging on A5

- State: closed
- URL: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/PTOAS/issues/421
- Created: 2026-04-02T02:51:57Z
- Updated: 2026-04-15T09:01:45Z
- Closed: 2026-04-15T09:01:44Z

### Body

When a `pto.tmov` instruction has the same source and destination (identity move), ptoas still treats it as a data-movement op and inserts sync instructions around it. These spurious syncs cause synchronization errors that hang the kernel on A5. The same code passes on A3 due to different sync behavior between the two platforms.

## Root Cause

ptoas unconditionally inserts sync instructions around every `pto.tmov`. When the tmov is a no-op (dst == src), the syncs are unnecessary and harmful.

## Suggested Fix

ptoas should detect identity `pto.tmov` instructions (where source and destination resolve to the same address/MemRef) and either:
1. Skip sync insertion for identity moves, or
2. Eliminate identity `pto.tmov` instructions entirely

## Reproducer

[fa5_softmax_rescale.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26403743/fa5_softmax_rescale.py)

## Related

- hw-native-sys/pypto#828 (original issue, filed on wrong repo)
- hw-native-sys/pypto#803
- hw-native-sys/pypto-lib#58

## Note

A complementary fix has been applied on the pypto side (hw-native-sys/pypto#836) to avoid emitting identity `pto.tmov` in the first place. However, ptoas should still handle this case defensively.

---

## #427 [Feature] pto.tmrgsort format2 should support 2-way and 3-way merge (currently hardcoded to 4-way)

- State: closed
- URL: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/PTOAS/issues/427
- Created: 2026-04-02T09:44:17Z
- Updated: 2026-04-09T03:53:23Z
- Closed: 2026-04-09T03:53:23Z

### Body

## Background

`pto.tmrgsort` currently has two formats:

- **format1**: single-list intra-block merge, `ins(src, blockLen)`
- **format2**: multi-list merge, **hardcoded to exactly 4 sources**, `ins(src0, src1, src2, src3)`

However, the underlying PTO-ISA `TMRGSORT` instruction supports 2-way, 3-way, and 4-way merges:

```
// 2-way
TMRGSORT(dst, executedNumList, tmp, src0, src1)
// 3-way
TMRGSORT(dst, executedNumList, tmp, src0, src1, src2)
// 4-way (currently supported)
TMRGSORT(dst, executedNumList, tmp, src0, src1, src2, src3)
```

## Current Limitation

`isFormat2()` hardcodes a 4-source requirement (`include/PTO/IR/PTOOps.td:3246`):

```cpp
bool isFormat2() { return getSrcs().size() == 4u && getDsts().size() == 2u && getExcuted(); }
```

The `print` function also hardcodes access to exactly 4 srcs (`lib/PTO/IR/PTO.cpp:4521-4524`).

Passing 2 or 3 sources triggers the catch-all verifier error:

```
tmrgsort expects format1 (1 src + blockLen + 1 dst) or format2 (4 srcs, outs dst, excuted)
```

## Expected Behavior

format2 should accept 2, 3, or 4 sources. The `isFormat2()` predicate should be relaxed to `srcs.size() >= 2 && srcs.size() <= 4`.

Assembly format would become variadic:

```mlir
// 2-way
pto.tmrgsort ins(%src0, %src1 {exhausted = false} : ...) outs(%dst, %tmp, %excuted : ...)

// 3-way
pto.tmrgsort ins(%src0, %src1, %src2 {exhausted = false} : ...) outs(%dst, %tmp, %excuted : ...)
```

## Layers Requiring Changes

- [ ] `include/PTO/IR/PTOOps.td` — relax `isFormat2()` predicate
- [ ] `lib/PTO/IR/PTO.cpp` — update `print`, `parse`, and `verify` to handle variable-length srcs
- [ ] `lib/PTO/Transforms/PTOViewToMemref.cpp` — update lowering patterns for variable-length srcs
- [ ] `docs/PTO_IR_manual.md` — update format2 assembly format description and examples
- [ ] `test/` — add regression tests for 2-way and 3-way cases

---

## #428 [Bug] generated C++ Cube kernel hangs with version >= 0.18

- State: closed
- URL: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/PTOAS/issues/428
- Created: 2026-04-02T10:08:21Z
- Updated: 2026-04-07T01:24:02Z
- Closed: 2026-04-07T01:24:02Z

### Body

### Component
EmitC / Codegen (lib/PTO/Transforms/PTOToEmitC.cpp)

### Description
The generated C++ in versions >= 0.18 appears to preserve the same overall math,
tensor views, and tensor layout for this kernel, but it changes the pipeline event
synchronization (`set_flag` / `wait_flag`) and tail synchronization behavior.

The version generated by 0.17 works for this reproducer. In that working output,
the event sequence is initialized before entering the loops, and the kernel ends
with explicit waits that drain the outstanding event dependencies.

In the >= 0.18 output, the synchronization schedule is different. In the failing
variant, the first main loop begins with:

  wait_flag(PIPE_M, PIPE_MTE1, EVENT_ID2);
  wait_flag(PIPE_M, PIPE_MTE1, EVENT_ID3);

but there is no obvious pre-loop:

  set_flag(PIPE_M, PIPE_MTE1, EVENT_ID3);

before that first wait on `EVENT_ID3`.

I compared the MLIR from the older working version and the newer failing version,
and for this kernel they appear identical in substance. The generated C++ differs
mainly in synchronization/event scheduling, which suggests the regression is
introduced downstream during EmitC/codegen or sync insertion rather than in the
high-level IR.

Reproducer archive:
[bug_reproduce.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26436355/bug_reproduce.zip)

### Reproduction

To fully reproduce see: https://github.com/huawei-csl/pto-dsl/tree/main/examples/aot/fast_inverse/block_inversion

```mlir
module {
  func.func @tri_inv_block2x2_fp16(%arg0: !pto.ptr<f32>, %arg1: !pto.ptr<f16>, %arg2: !pto.ptr<f16>, %arg3: i32) {
    pto.section.cube {
      %c0 = arith.constant 0 : index
      %c1 = arith.constant 1 : index
      %c64 = arith.constant 64 : index
      %c32 = arith.constant 32 : index
      %0 = arith.index_cast %arg3 : i32 to index
      %1 = arith.subi %0, %c1 : index
      %2 = pto.get_block_idx
      %3 = arith.index_cast %2 : i64 to index
      %4 = pto.get_block_num
      %5 = arith.index_cast %4 : i64 to index
      %6 = arith.muli %5, %c64 : index
      %7 = arith.muli %3, %c64 : index
      %8 = arith.addi %7, %c32 : index
      %9 = pto.make_tensor_view %arg1, shape = [%6, %c64], strides = [%c64, %c1] : !pto.tensor_view<?x?xf16>
      %10 = pto.make_tensor_view %arg0, shape = [%6, %c64], strides = [%c64, %c1] : !pto.tensor_view<?x?xf32>
      %11 = pto.make_tensor_view %arg2, shape = [%c32, %c32], strides = [%c32, %c1] : !pto.tensor_view<?x?xf16>
      %12 = pto.partition_view %11, offsets = [%c0, %c0], sizes = [%c32, %c32] : !pto.tensor_view<?x?xf16> -> !pto.partition_tensor_view<32x32xf16>
      %13 = pto.partition_view %9, offsets = [%7, %c0], sizes = [%c32, %c32] : !pto.tensor_view<?x?xf16> -> !pto.partition_tensor_view<32x32xf16>
      %14 = pto.partition_view %9, offsets = [%8, %c0], sizes = [%c32, %c32] : !pto.tensor_view<?x?xf16> -> !pto.partition_tensor_view<32x32xf16>
      %15 = pto.partition_view %9, offsets = [%8, %c32], sizes = [%c32, %c32] : !pto.tensor_view<?x?xf16> -> !pto.partition_tensor_view<32x32xf16>
      %16 = pto.partition_view %10, offsets = [%7, %c0], sizes = [%c32, %c32] : !pto.tensor_view<?x?xf32> -> !pto.partition_tensor_view<32x32xf32>
      %17 = pto.partition_view %10, offsets = [%8, %c0], sizes = [%c32, %c32] : !pto.tensor_view<?x?xf32> -> !pto.partition_tensor_view<32x32xf32>
      %18 = pto.partition_view %10, offsets = [%8, %c32], sizes = [%c32, %c32] : !pto.tensor_view<?x?xf32> -> !pto.partition_tensor_view<32x32xf32>
      %19 = pto.alloc_tile : !pto.tile_buf<loc=mat, dtype=f16, rows=32, cols=32, v_row=32, v_col=32, blayout=col_major, slayout=row_major, fractal=512, pad=0>

      pto.tstore ins(%29 : !pto.tile_buf<loc=acc, dtype=f32, rows=32, cols=32, v_row=32, v_col=32, blayout=col_major, slayout=row_major, fractal=1024, pad=0>) outs(%17 : !pto.partition_tensor_view<32x32xf32>)
    }
    return
  }
}


```
Use the MLIR snippet in the reproducer and run:

  ptoas --enable-insert-sync inverse.pto -o inverse.cpp

Additional note:
The MLIR for the working and failing versions appears unchanged for this kernel.
The generated C++ differs mainly in event scheduling and tail synchronization.

### Expected behavior
The generated C++ should preserve a valid event schedule for the kernel, matching
the behavior of the previously working version.

In particular:
- every `wait_flag(...)` should have a matching earlier `set_flag(...)`
- events used inside loops should be properly initialized before the first iteration
- end-of-kernel synchronization should ensure all pending work is finished
- enabling `--enable-insert-sync` should not introduce hangs, invalid waits, or
  nondeterministic behavior

### Actual behavior / error logs
The generated C++ has a different synchronization schedule from the previously
working output.

In the failing generated version, the first main loop contains:

  wait_flag(PIPE_M, PIPE_MTE1, EVENT_ID2);
  wait_flag(PIPE_M, PIPE_MTE1, EVENT_ID3);

but there is no obvious earlier pre-loop:

  set_flag(PIPE_M, PIPE_MTE1, EVENT_ID3);

before the first iteration.

The old working version did not have this issue and used a fully initialized and
explicitly drained event schedule.

This appears to cause invalid synchronization behavior in the generated kernel,
potentially resulting in:
- hang / deadlock
- dependence on stale event state
- nondeterministic execution

Tail behavior also changed.

Old working version ended with:

  pipe_barrier(PIPE_ALL);
  wait_flag(PIPE_M, PIPE_MTE1, EVENT_ID2);
  wait_flag(PIPE_FIX, PIPE_M, EVENT_ID2);
  wait_flag(PIPE_M, PIPE_MTE1, EVENT_ID7);
  wait_flag(PIPE_FIX, PIPE_M, EVENT_ID6);

The failing generated version instead ends with:

  ptoas_auto_sync_tail(PTOAutoSyncTailMode::kBarrierAll);

which lowers to a barrier-only path and no longer explicitly drains those event
dependencies in the same way.

## #441 A5 target hangs on RMSNorm vector kernel that passes on A2A3

- State: closed
- URL: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/PTOAS/issues/441
- Created: 2026-04-03T09:14:54Z
- Updated: 2026-04-15T09:01:34Z
- Closed: 2026-04-15T09:01:34Z

### Body

## Problem

A PTO-IR vector kernel (`decode_projection_incore_0.pto`) compiles and runs correctly when targeting **A2A3**, but **hangs at runtime** when compiled for **A5**.

## Environment

- **PTOAS version**: 0.22

## Reproduction

PTO file attached below.

[decode_projection_incore_0.pto.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26457179/decode_projection_incore_0.pto.txt)
[rmsnorm_incore_0.pto.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26457180/rmsnorm_incore_0.pto.txt)

Steps:
1. Change `pto.target_arch` from `"a2a3"` to `"a5"` in the module attributes
2. Compile with `ptoas`
3. Run on A5 platform — program **hangs indefinitely** (no crash, no error)

## Behavior

| Target | Compile | Run |
|--------|---------|-----|
| A2A3 | OK | OK |
| A5 | OK | **Hangs** |

## Kernel Summary

This is a **RMSNorm vector kernel** (`decode_projection_incore_0`) from the Qwen3-32B decode layer projection. It operates on `[16, 5120]` BF16 input with `K_CHUNK=128` (40 iterations):

1. **Loop 1** — accumulate squared partial sums: `tload` → `tcvt`(bf16→f32) → `tmul`(x²) → `trowsum` → `tadd` (accumulate) → `tmov`
2. **Post-loop** — compute inv_rms: `tmuls`(÷5120) → `tadds`(+ε) → `trsqrt`
3. **Loop 2** — apply normalization: `tload` → `tcvt` → `trowexpandmul`(×inv_rms) → `tcolexpandmul`(×γ) → `tcvt`(f32→bf16) → `tstore`

## Operations Used

`tload`, `tstore`, `tcvt`, `tmul`, `trowsum`, `tadd`, `tmov`, `tmuls`, `tadds`, `trsqrt`, `trowexpandmul`, `tcolexpandmul`, `texpands`

## PTO File

<!-- Please attach the .pto file here -->

## Context

Discovered during E2E validation of `pypto-lib` Qwen3-32B decode tilelet (hw-native-sys/pypto-lib#58, Scope 1).

## #454 [Bug] WidenEventId places loop 2's wait_flag outside the loop instead of inside it

- State: closed
- URL: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/PTOAS/issues/454
- Created: 2026-04-07T14:59:34Z
- Updated: 2026-04-08T09:57:14Z
- Closed: 2026-04-08T09:57:14Z

### Body

### Component

EmitC / Codegen (lib/PTO/Transforms/PTOToEmitC.cpp)

### Description

The fix in PR #443 (commit 7198be3) works correctly when a function has a single loop, but breaks when two independent loops exist in the same function. Because both loops use the same pipe pair, PTOAS sees that the pipe pair is already claimed by loop 1 and skips setting up proper guards for loop 2. The result: the set and wait are both placed outside the loop and immediately cancel each other out, leaving the loop body running with no synchronization at all.

### Reproduction (minimal)

The zip contains three files compiled from the same input: the working 0.09 output, the broken 0.24 output, and a hand-corrected working 0.24 version.

In 0.24, a wait instruction for the second loop is placed outside the loop and immediately consumed before entering the loop, so the loop never actually waits. The fix moves it inside the loop where it should belong. See the diff:

```bash
$ diff inverse_0_24.cpp inverse_0_24_fixed.cpp 
185d184
<   wait_flag(PIPE_M, PIPE_MTE1, EVENT_ID7);
187a187
>     wait_flag(PIPE_M, PIPE_MTE1, EVENT_ID7);
215a216
>     set_flag(PIPE_M, PIPE_MTE1, EVENT_ID7);
261a263
>   wait_flag(PIPE_M, PIPE_MTE1, EVENT_ID7);
```

[bug_reproduce.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26543887/bug_reproduce.zip)

```mlir
      %c0 = arith.constant 0 : index
```

### Expected behavior

`set_flag(PIPE_M, PIPE_MTE1, EVENT_IDx)` is emitted immediately before each loop starts, and the matching wait_flag is placed as the first instruction inside the loop body, so each iteration waits for the previous one's signal before proceeding.

### Actual behavior / error logs

`set_flag(PIPE_M, PIPE_MTE1, EVENT_ID7)` is correctly placed immediately before loop 2, but the matching wait_flag is placed right after it — also outside the loop. The two instructions cancel each other out immediately, and the loop body runs with no synchronization guard at all.

## #464 [Bug] ptoas reports error with pl.full(shape, dtype=BF16, value)

- State: closed
- URL: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/PTOAS/issues/464
- Created: 2026-04-09T08:44:05Z
- Updated: 2026-04-09T12:31:17Z
- Closed: 2026-04-09T12:29:08Z

### Body

### Component

Verifier / IR semantics (lib/PTO/IR)

### Description

Calling `pl.full(shape, dtype=BF16, value)` results in an error in PTOAS. The intent is to create a tensor of the specified shape in BF16 format filled with the given value. Error occurs even with valid input arguments.

### Reproduction (minimal)

```markdown
import pl
pl.full((2, 2), dtype=BF16, value=1.0)

# Observe the error reported by ptoas.
```

### Expected behavior

`pl.full` should work correctly and generate a tensor of the given shape and value with dtype BF16, without returning an error.

### Actual behavior / error logs

```text
- when use value = 0.0

.pto file:

  %c0 = arith.constant 0 : index
  pto.texpands ins(%c0 : index) outs(%mlp_zero_chunk__tile : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=bf16, rows=16, cols=64, v_row=16, v_col=64, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>)


error shown:

Failed to compile function 'scope3_incore_4': ptoas compilation failed: loc("build_output/Qwen3Scope3_20260409_160058/ptoas/scope3_incore_4.pto":15:5): error: 'pto.texpands' op expects scalar type == dst element type


- when use value = 0

.pto file:

  %cst = arith.constant 0.000000e+00 : f32
  pto.texpands ins(%cst : f32) outs(%mlp_zero_chunk__tile : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, rows=16, cols=64, v_row=16, v_col=64, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>)


error shown:

Failed to compile function 'scope3_incore_4': ptoas compilation failed: loc("build_output/Qwen3Scope3_20260409_160258/ptoas/scope3_incore_4.pto":14:5): error: 'pto.texpands' op operand #0 must be numeric (integer/float), but got 'index'
```

## #470 [Feature] 支持 fillpad_inplace 基于同地址判断

- State: closed
- URL: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/PTOAS/issues/470
- Created: 2026-04-10T07:19:12Z
- Updated: 2026-04-15T03:32:28Z
- Closed: 2026-04-15T03:32:28Z

### Body

### Summary

目前 PTOAS 在 lowering pto.tfillpad 时，如果判断 src == dst，就会直接选择生成 TFILLPAD_INPLACE。但从 ISA 侧实现来看，FILLPAD_INPLACE 在运行时会同时读取src.GetValidRow()/GetValidCol()、dst.GetValidRow()/GetValidCol()，这意味着它实际上依赖的是src 提供原始有效区边界，dst 提供目标填充范围边界。TFILLPAD_INPLACE 的合理语义不应简单理解为“同一个 tile value 的 fillpad”，而应理解为：
      1.src 和 dst 指向同一块底层地址
      2.原地 padding
而当前的ptoas语义， src 和 dst 是同一个 tile 对象，它们的 validshape 通常相同，pto.tfillpad(tileA, tileA)转换成底层cce表达TFILLPAD_INPLACE（tileA, tileA)，实际运行并没有执行任何填充操作。

### Motivation / use case

a5功能

是否可以改为根据src或者dst同地址进行判断，或者显示支持pto.tfillpad_inplace

_No response_

## #487 [Bug] --pto-arch=a5 may mis-verify pto.tsel(i8) as A2/A3 during parse-time verifier

- State: closed
- URL: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/PTOAS/issues/487
- Created: 2026-04-15T08:38:21Z
- Updated: 2026-04-15T09:46:41Z
- Closed: 2026-04-15T09:46:41Z

### Body

### Component

PTO IR verifier / parser arch dispatch

### Description

When compiling textual `.pto` without module-level `pto.target_arch`, using `--pto-arch=a5` can still mis-verify `pto.tsel(i8)` as A2/A3 during parse-time verification:

`'pto.tsel' op expects A2/A3 tsel src0, src1, and dst element type to be i16/i32/f16/f32`

A5 is expected to accept i8 for `pto.tsel`.

I built a minimal reproducer with 2 `func.func` ops, each containing only `alloc_tile + pto.tsel(i8)`.

### Reproduction (minimal)

Reproducer file:

`test/repro/issue_tls_arch_tsel_i8_min.pto`

Command:

`build/tools/ptoas/ptoas --pto-arch=a5 test/repro/issue_tls_arch_tsel_i8_min.pto -o -`

### Expected behavior

`pto.tsel(i8)` should pass verifier on A5.

### Actual behavior / error logs

```text
loc("test/repro/issue_tls_arch_tsel_i8_min.pto":21:5): error: 'pto.tsel' op expects A2/A3 tsel src0, src1, and dst element type to be i16/i32/f16/f32
loc("test/repro/issue_tls_arch_tsel_i8_min.pto":34:5): error: 'pto.tsel' op expects A2/A3 tsel src0, src1, and dst element type to be i16/i32/f16/f32
Error: Failed to parse MLIR.
```

### Control experiment

If I add module attr explicitly:

`module attributes {"pto.target_arch" = "a5"} { ... }`

Then run:

`build/tools/ptoas/ptoas test/repro/issue_tls_arch_tsel_i8_min_attr.pto -o -`

the `A2/A3 tsel` verifier error disappears.

### Suspected root cause

`getVerifierTargetArch()` falls back to `getPTOParserTargetArch()` when module attr is not yet visible.

`getPTOParserTargetArch()` uses thread-local storage. MLIR parser verifies immediately after parse (`verifyAfterParse=true`) and verifier parallelizes `IsolatedFromAbove` children. Since `func.func` is `IsolatedFromAbove`, some op verifiers run on worker threads and may read default TLS arch (Unspecified/A3), causing wrong A2/A3 dispatch.

### Environment

- Repo: `hw-native-sys/PTOAS`
- Local branch: feature-vpto-backend
- Local commit: f4c679ae9916d586211199adf42025977f574f9e
- Tool: gh version 2.45.0 (2025-07-18 Ubuntu 2.45.0-1ubuntu0.3)


### Inline minimal test case



### Copy-paste repro commands

```bash
cat > /tmp/issue_tls_arch_tsel_i8_min.pto <<"EOF"
// Minimal reproducer: parser-time arch fallback reads non-A5 and mis-verifies pto.tsel(i8) as A2/A3.
//
// Repro command:
//   build/tools/ptoas/ptoas --pto-arch=a5 test/repro/issue_tls_arch_tsel_i8_min.pto -o -
//
// Actual (unexpected on A5):
//   error: 'pto.tsel' op expects A2/A3 tsel src0, src1, and dst element type to be i16/i32/f16/f32
//
// Control:
//   Add module attr: module attributes {"pto.target_arch" = "a5"} { ... }
//   Then the above verifier error disappears.

module {
  func.func @f0() {
    %mask = pto.alloc_tile : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=i8, rows=2, cols=128, v_row=2, v_col=128, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>
    %src0 = pto.alloc_tile : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=i8, rows=2, cols=128, v_row=2, v_col=128, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>
    %src1 = pto.alloc_tile : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=i8, rows=2, cols=128, v_row=2, v_col=128, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>
    %tmp  = pto.alloc_tile : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=i8, rows=1, cols=64, v_row=1, v_col=64, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>
    %dst  = pto.alloc_tile : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=i8, rows=2, cols=128, v_row=2, v_col=128, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>

    pto.tsel ins(%mask, %src0, %src1, %tmp : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=i8, rows=2, cols=128, v_row=2, v_col=128, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>, !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=i8, rows=2, cols=128, v_row=2, v_col=128, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>, !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=i8, rows=2, cols=128, v_row=2, v_col=128, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>, !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=i8, rows=1, cols=64, v_row=1, v_col=64, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>)
             outs(%dst : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=i8, rows=2, cols=128, v_row=2, v_col=128, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>)
    return
  }

  // Keep >=2 functions to trigger verifier's IsolatedFromAbove parallel branch.
  func.func @f1() {
    %mask = pto.alloc_tile : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=i8, rows=2, cols=128, v_row=2, v_col=128, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>
    %src0 = pto.alloc_tile : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=i8, rows=2, cols=128, v_row=2, v_col=128, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>
    %src1 = pto.alloc_tile : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=i8, rows=2, cols=128, v_row=2, v_col=128, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>
    %tmp  = pto.alloc_tile : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=i8, rows=1, cols=64, v_row=1, v_col=64, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>
    %dst  = pto.alloc_tile : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=i8, rows=2, cols=128, v_row=2, v_col=128, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>

    pto.tsel ins(%mask, %src0, %src1, %tmp : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=i8, rows=2, cols=128, v_row=2, v_col=128, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>, !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=i8, rows=2, cols=128, v_row=2, v_col=128, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>, !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=i8, rows=2, cols=128, v_row=2, v_col=128, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>, !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=i8, rows=1, cols=64, v_row=1, v_col=64, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>)
             outs(%dst : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=i8, rows=2, cols=128, v_row=2, v_col=128, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>)
    return
  }
}
EOF
build/tools/ptoas/ptoas --pto-arch=a5 /tmp/issue_tls_arch_tsel_i8_min.pto -o -
```

## #488 [Feature] Support multiple cross-core pipes per Cube/Vector function

- State: closed
- URL: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/PTOAS/issues/488
- Created: 2026-04-15T08:42:39Z
- Updated: 2026-05-28T03:00:00Z
- Closed: 2026-04-30T07:01:58Z

### Body

### Summary

  Could PTOAS support more than one cross-core pipe per Cube/Vector function?

  In our mixed-kernel flow, an AIC/AIV function pair may need bidirectional communication. Today this appears to be modeled as a single frontend `initialize_pipe` per function,
  and when both directions are needed it lowers to one `DIR_BOTH` pipe. As a result, the available pipe capacity is effectively shared by C2V and V2C instead of having two
  independent directional pipes.

### Motivation / use case

  After mixed-kernel splitting in PyPTO, we may end up with both of these directions in the same Cube/Vector function pair:

  - AIC -> AIV transfers (`tpush_to_aiv` / `tpop_from_aic`)
  - AIV -> AIC transfers (`tpush_to_aic` / `tpop_from_aiv`)

  The current restriction seems to be that each Cube/Vector kernel can only have at most one pipe init. So if both directions are present, we have to use one bidirectional pipe
  and split its capacity between the two directions.

  What we would ideally like instead is:

  - one C2V pipe for AIC -> AIV
  - one V2C pipe for AIV -> AIC

  That would avoid the current "one pipe shared by both directions" limitation.

### Proposed API / behavior

  Ideally, PTOAS could allow multiple frontend pipe instances for the same function pair, for example two separate pipes in a bidirectional case:

  ```mlir
  // Cube side
  pto.aic_initialize_pipe {dir_mask = 1, slot_size = ...} (...)
  pto.aic_initialize_pipe {dir_mask = 2, slot_size = ...} (...)

  // Vector side
  pto.aiv_initialize_pipe {dir_mask = 1, slot_size = ...} (...)
  pto.aiv_initialize_pipe {dir_mask = 2, slot_size = ...} (...)
  ```

  I realize this likely requires some way for tpush / tpop / tfree ops to identify which pipe they belong to, because the current frontend transfer ops do not carry an explicit
  pipe handle.

  If supporting multiple pipes is not the intended direction, could you clarify whether the limitation comes from:

  - the current PTOAS frontend IR / lowering design,
  - pto-isa,
  - or a lower-level software / hardware constraint?

### Alternatives considered

  The current workaround is to use a single `dir_mask = 3` pipe for both directions. This is functionally workable, but it forces C2V and V2C to share one pipe instead of using two
  independent directional pipes.

### Additional context

  From reading the current PTOAS design and lowering code, my understanding is:

  - frontend tpush / tpop / tfree ops do not carry a pipe operand / handle,
  - PTOAS currently enforces at most one `pto.aic_initialize_pipe` or `pto.aiv_initialize_pipe` per function,
  - when `dir_mask = 3`, both frontend directions are bound to the same internal `DIR_BOTH` pipe.

  So the main question is whether this is only a current frontend/lowering design choice, or whether there is some deeper reason that makes multiple pipes per Cube/Vector
  function impossible or undesirable.

---

## #489 [Feature] Support interleaved tpop/tfree schedules on a single pipe

- State: closed
- URL: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/PTOAS/issues/489
- Created: 2026-04-15T09:01:29Z
- Updated: 2026-05-28T02:59:19Z
- Closed: 2026-04-16T07:36:58Z

### Body

### Summary

  Could PTOAS support interleaved consumer schedules for `tpop` / `tfree` on the same pipe, instead of requiring the current strict pattern:

  `tpop -> use -> tfree -> next tpop`

  What we would like to enable is a double-buffered style schedule where a consumer can prefetch the next tile before the current tile is freed, so that `tpop` and `use` have a chance to overlap.

### Motivation / use case

  In our mixed-kernel flow, the consumer side of a cross-core pipe is currently forced into a serialized pattern:

  1. `tpop` one tile
  2. use that tile
  3. `tfree`
  4. only then issue the next `tpop`

  This prevents interleaved schedules such as:

  ```mlir
  %t0 = pto.tpop(%tile0, %pipe) {split = 0}
  %t1 = pto.tpop(%tile1, %pipe) {split = 0}

  use(%t0)
  use(%t1)

  pto.tfree(%pipe) {split = 0}
  pto.tfree(%pipe) {split = 0}

  or loop-pipelined forms like:

  %curr = pto.tpop(%tile0, %pipe) {split = 0}
  scf.for ... {
    %next = pto.tpop(%tile1, %pipe) {split = 0}   // prefetch next tile
    use(%curr)
    pto.tfree(%pipe) {split = 0}
    %curr = %next
  }
  ```

  Supporting this kind of schedule would make double buffering possible on the consumer side, and may expose overlap / latency-hiding opportunities between tpop and compute.

### Proposed API / behavior

  At a minimum, it would be useful to support more than one outstanding tpop on the same pipe, as long as the frees are still explicit and balanced.

  However, from reading the current PTOAS IR and passes, it looks like the main limitation is that pto.tfree only carries pipe_handle, not the identity of the borrowed tile / slot. So if interleaved schedules are to be supported, PTOAS may need one of these directions:

  - make tfree target a specific borrowed tile or pop token, instead of only a pipe handle
  - introduce an explicit borrow / token result from tpop
  - or use some other internal representation that can distinguish multiple outstanding consumer slots on the same pipe

### Alternatives considered

  The current workaround is to keep the strict serialized pattern:

  tpop -> use -> tfree -> next tpop

  This is functionally correct, but it prevents consumer-side double buffering and any possible overlap between prefetching the next tile and using the current tile.

### Additional context

  From the current PTOAS code, this restriction appears to be intentional today:

  - PTOVerifyTFree rejects: multiple outstanding pops on the same pipe are not supported
  - pto.tfree is defined as releasing the current consumer slot for a pipe, and it only takes pipe_handle
  - frontend tfree_from_aic / tfree_from_aiv also lower to pto.tfree(%pipe) without carrying tile identity

  So the main question is:

  Is it feasible to support interleaved / double-buffered tpop consumer schedules in PTOAS, or is there a deeper constraint in EmitC / pto-isa / lower-level software or hardware that fundamentally requires only one outstanding consumer pop per pipe?

---

- Created: 2026-04-16T19:31:42Z
- Updated: 2026-04-23T12:15:01Z
- Closed: 

### Body

### Component

PTO Dialect / ODS (include/PTO/IR)

### Description

The following mlir for standard Flash Attention might not use all vector cores. How can I improve it? The biggest difference with [pto-isa fa_performance kernel ](https://gitcode.com/cann/pto-isa/blob/master/kernels/manual/common/flash_atten/fa_performance_kernel.cpp?init=initTree)is the lack of `TMpipe` and `subblock` indexing for vector cores, which I tried to implement without success due to probably the lack of entry_offset for `TPush` and `Tpop` in the dialect.
Here you can find the [PTO-DSL](https://github.com/huawei-csl/pto-dsl/pull/112) code that generates the following MLIR.

### Reproduction (minimal)

```mlir
module {
  func.func @cube_kernel(%arg0: !pto.ptr<f32>, %arg1: !pto.ptr<f16>, %arg2: !pto.ptr<f16>, %arg3: !pto.ptr<f16>) attributes {pto.kernel_kind = #pto.kernel_kind<cube>} {
    %c0 = arith.constant 0 : index
    %c1 = arith.constant 1 : index
    %c32 = arith.constant 32 : index
    %c32_0 = arith.constant 32 : index
    %c256 = arith.constant 256 : index
    %c8192 = arith.constant 8192 : index
    %c32_1 = arith.constant 32 : index
    %c64 = arith.constant 64 : index
    %0 = pto.get_block_num

```


To reproduce, the generated cpp requires some manual fixes. See the perl lines in this shell script:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
ARTIFACT_DIR="${SCRIPT_DIR}/build_artifacts"
MLIR_PATH="${ARTIFACT_DIR}/fa_gen.mlir"
GENERATED_CPP="${ARTIFACT_DIR}/fa_gen.cpp"
LIB_PATH="${ARTIFACT_DIR}/fa_lib.so"

PTO_LIB_PATH="${PTO_LIB_PATH:-/sources/pto-isa}"

mkdir -p "${ARTIFACT_DIR}"
rm -f "${GENERATED_CPP}" "${LIB_PATH}"

python "${SCRIPT_DIR}/kernels/fa_builder.py" > "${MLIR_PATH}"
# No --enable-insert-sync: the DSL builder inserts explicit sync primitives.
ptoas --pto-arch=a3 --enable-insert-sync "${MLIR_PATH}" > "${GENERATED_CPP}"

# Per-block GM-slot partitioning: TPipe does NOT offset the GM slot buffer by
# block_idx.  All blocks would share the same 8 GM slots, corrupting each
# other's c2v/v2c data.  We inject an offset into call_both so that each block
# gets its own 8-slot region.
#
# Offset = SLOTS_PER_BLOCK * SLOT_SIZE / sizeof(float)
#        = 8 * (S0 * max(S1_TILE, HEAD) * 4) / 4
#        = 8 * S0 * max(S1_TILE, HEAD)
#        = 8 * 32 * 256 = 65536  fp32 elements
GM_ELEMS_PER_BLOCK=$(python3 -c "
S0, HEAD, S1_TILE, SLOTS_PER_BLOCK = 32, 32, 256, 8
print(SLOTS_PER_BLOCK * S0 * max(S1_TILE, HEAD))
")
perl -pi -e "s/  cube_kernel\\(v2,/  __gm__ float* gm_per_blk = v2 + get_block_idx() * ${GM_ELEMS_PER_BLOCK};\\n  cube_kernel(gm_per_blk,/" "${GENERATED_CPP}"
perl -pi -e "s/  vector_kernel\\(v2,/  vector_kernel(gm_per_blk,/" "${GENERATED_CPP}"

bisheng \
    -I"${PTO_LIB_PATH}/include" \
    -fPIC -shared -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=2 -O2 -std=c++17 \
    -Wno-macro-redefined -Wno-ignored-attributes -fstack-protector-strong \
    -xcce -Xhost-start -Xhost-end \
    -mllvm -cce-aicore-stack-size=0x8000 \
    -mllvm -cce-aicore-function-stack-size=0x8000 \
    -mllvm -cce-aicore-record-overflow=true \
    -mllvm -cce-aicore-addr-transform \
    -mllvm -cce-aicore-dcci-insert-for-scalar=false \
    --npu-arch=dav-2201 -DMEMORY_BASE \
    -std=gnu++17 \
    -DKERNEL_CPP="\"${GENERATED_CPP}\"" \
    "${SCRIPT_DIR}/caller.cpp" \
    -o "${LIB_PATH}"

echo "Generated ${GENERATED_CPP}."
echo "Built ${LIB_PATH}."
```

These two lines are currently needed for a bug in addptr, see #497 
```bash
perl -pi -e "s/  cube_kernel\\(v2,/  __gm__ float* gm_per_blk = v2 + get_block_idx() * ${GM_ELEMS_PER_BLOCK};\\n  cube_kernel(gm_per_blk,/" "${GENERATED_CPP}"
perl -pi -e "s/  vector_kernel\\(v2,/  vector_kernel(gm_per_blk,/" "${GENERATED_CPP}"
```

### Expected behavior

the generated kernel should use all 48 vector cores on A3

### Actual behavior / error logs

No errors to show, the generated kernel matches the torch npu fused attention reference, but it is way slower:

```bash

  blockDim=24  Q-blocks=64  cores=24
  warmup=10  iters=100

  npu_fused_attn:   174.37 us  (12315.91 GFLOP/s)

    kernel         max|err|=1.79e-05  mean|err|=2.87e-06
    npu_fused_attn max|err|=3.46e-05  mean|err|=4.09e-06
============================================================
```

## #506 [Bug] pto.tdivs scalar-first syntax loses direction in mainline (ins(%scalar, %src) normalized)

- State: closed
- URL: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/PTOAS/issues/506
- Created: 2026-04-17T08:12:02Z
- Updated: 2026-04-20T11:58:35Z
- Closed: 2026-04-20T11:58:35Z

### Body

### Component

PTO Dialect / `TDivSOp` parser + canonical operand handling (`lib/PTO/IR/PTO.cpp`)

### Description

`pto.tdivs` loses operand direction semantics for textual form `ins(%scalar, %src)`.

Both forms:
- `ins(%src, %scalar)`
- `ins(%scalar, %src)`

are normalized to the same internal operand order `(tile, scalar, dst)`, so `scalar / src` cannot be represented.

### Minimal reproduction (mainline, no VPTO flags)

Input file: `test/dsl/issue_117_repro.pto`

```mlir
module {
  func.func @TDIVS_SRC_SCALAR() {
    %a = pto.alloc_tile : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, rows=16, cols=64, v_row=16, v_col=64,
                                        blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>
    %dst = pto.alloc_tile : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, rows=16, cols=64, v_row=16, v_col=64,
                                          blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>
    %scalar = arith.constant 2.0 : f32
    pto.tdivs ins(%a, %scalar : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, rows=16, cols=64, v_row=16, v_col=64,
                               blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>, f32)
              outs(%dst : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, rows=16, cols=64, v_row=16, v_col=64,
                                        blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>)
    return
  }

  func.func @TDIVS_SCALAR_SRC() {
    %a = pto.alloc_tile : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, rows=16, cols=64, v_row=16, v_col=64,
                                        blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>
    %dst = pto.alloc_tile : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, rows=16, cols=64, v_row=16, v_col=64,
                                          blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>
    %scalar = arith.constant 2.0 : f32
    pto.tdivs ins(%scalar, %a : f32,
                               !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, rows=16, cols=64, v_row=16, v_col=64,
                               blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>)
              outs(%dst : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, rows=16, cols=64, v_row=16, v_col=64,
                                        blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>)
    return
  }
}
```

Run command (mainline-compatible):

```bash
ptoas --pto-arch=a5 test/dsl/issue_117_repro.pto > build/issue117_mainline.out 2> build/issue117_mainline.log
```

### Expected behavior

- `TDIVS_SRC_SCALAR` keeps `src / scalar`
- `TDIVS_SCALAR_SRC` keeps `scalar / src`

### Actual behavior

In `build/issue117_mainline.log`, both functions are normalized to the same textual op shape:

```text
func.func @TDIVS_SRC_SCALAR() { ... pto.tdivs ins(%0, %cst : ..., f32) ... }
func.func @TDIVS_SCALAR_SRC() { ... pto.tdivs ins(%0, %cst : ..., f32) ... }
```

This indicates `ins(%scalar, %src)` direction is not preserved.

### Suspected root cause

`TDivSOp::parse` accepts both input orders but stores operands in canonical `(src, scalar, dst)` order by swapping when scalar appears first. Downstream passes therefore cannot distinguish the two semantic directions.

### Environment

- Repo: `hw-native-sys/PTOAS` (official)
- Arch: `a5`
- Command: `ptoas --pto-arch=a5 test/dsl/issue_117_repro.pto`

## #522 [Bug] pto.tcolexpanddiv rejects i16/i32 on A5 during verification

- State: closed
- URL: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/PTOAS/issues/522
- Created: 2026-04-20T09:00:04Z
- Updated: 2026-04-21T11:25:07Z
- Closed: 2026-04-21T11:25:07Z

### Body

### Component

Verifier / IR semantics (lib/PTO/IR)

### Description

`pto.tcolexpanddiv` currently rejects integer element types during MLIR verification. On `official/main`, the verifier only accepts `f16` and `f32`, but A5 integer cases with `i16` and `i32` are expected by downstream tests and by the existing `tdiv` verifier behavior.

I confirmed this on `official/main` by checking `TColExpandDivOp::verify()`:

- `verifyTColExpandBinaryLikeOp(..., /*allowIntegerTypes=*/false)` is used for `pto.tcolexpanddiv`
- the shared helper only allows `i16/i32` when `allowIntegerTypes=true`

As a result, minimal IR with `dtype=i32` fails before tile-op-expand / lowering.

### Reproduction (minimal)

```mlir
module {
  func.func @tcolexpanddiv_i32_issue() {
    %src0 = pto.alloc_tile
      : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=i32, rows=16, cols=32, v_row=16, v_col=32,
                      blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>
    %src1 = pto.alloc_tile
      : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=i32, rows=1, cols=32, v_row=1, v_col=32,
                      blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>
    %dst = pto.alloc_tile
      : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=i32, rows=16, cols=32, v_row=16, v_col=32,
                      blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>

    pto.tcolexpanddiv ins(%src0, %src1 : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=i32, rows=16, cols=32, v_row=16, v_col=32,
                                blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>,
                            !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=i32, rows=1, cols=32, v_row=1, v_col=32,
                                blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>)
               outs(%dst : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=i32, rows=16, cols=32, v_row=16, v_col=32,
                                     blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>)
    return
  }
}
```

```bash
./build/tools/ptoas/ptoas \
  --pto-arch=a5 \
  --pto-backend=vpto \
  --enable-tile-op-expand \
  --vpto-emit-hivm-llvm \
  test/dsl/issue_140_repro.pto
```

Local repro file:
- `test/dsl/issue_140_repro.pto`

### Expected behavior

`pto.tcolexpanddiv` should accept `i16` and `i32` on A5, instead of rejecting them during verification. Integer division semantics should match the intended integer divide behavior for this op.

### Actual behavior / error logs


## #527 [Feature] PTOAS 支持 pto-isa 中的Layout::NZ 推断

- State: open
- URL: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/PTOAS/issues/527
- Created: 2026-04-21T02:16:42Z
- Updated: 2026-05-20T01:42:44Z
- Closed: 

### Body

### Summary

当前 PTOAS 的 Layout::NZ 推断规则，与 pto-isa 中已经定义的标准化NZ 五维表示不一致。对于 pto-isa 侧合法的NZ 五维 tensor_view，PTOAS 当前不会将其推断为 Layout::NZ，而是推断成 Layout::ND。
1.pto-isa 当前对 2D 的五维NZ 的定义：
TileShape2D<T, rows, cols, Layout::NZ> / BaseShape2D<T, rows, cols, Layout::NZ> 对二维逻辑 tensor 的五维表示为：
     shape  = [1, cols / c0, rows / 16, 16, c0]
     stride = [rows * cols, rows * c0, 16 * c0, c0, 1]
     c0 = 32 / sizeof(dtype)
例如 fp32 且 (rows, cols) = (128, 64) 时：
      shape  = [1, 8, 8, 16, 8]
      stride = [8192, 1024, 128, 8, 1]
这套定义是 pto-isa 中二维NZ的五维表示的标准形式。
2.PTOAS 当前的 NZ 推断规则
当前 PTOAS 在右对齐到五维后，判定 Layout::NZ 的关键条件是：
      shape3 == 16
      shape3 * shape4 * elemBytes == 512
      stride5 == 1
      stride4 == shape5
当前不一致现象,使用附件可进行复现：
①用例一，pto-isa canonical 2D NZ 五维形式：
      shape  = [1, 8, 8, 16, 8]
      stride = [8192, 1024, 128, 8, 1]
PTOAS 生成的 C++ 中是 pto::Layout::ND
②用例二，当前 PTOAS NZ 推断规则的五维形式
       shape = [4, 1, 16, 8, 16]
       stride = [2048, 2048, 128, 16, 1]
PTOAS 生成的 C++ 中是 pto::Layout::NZ
说明当前PTOAS 还不能把 pto-isa 的二维 NZ 的五维形式推断成 Layout::NZ

[nz_store_probe.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26916670/nz_store_probe.py)

### Motivation / use case

a5功能

### Proposed API / behavior

希望在现有的基础上，支持将 pto-isa 中的二维NZ 的五维 tensor_view / partition_tensor_view 推断为 Layout::NZ

### Alternatives considered

_No response_

### Additional context

_No response_
