## #1051 [VPTO][PTODSL TileLib] Support 1D/2D template selection for all element-wise TileOps

- State: closed
- URL: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/PTOAS/issues/1051
- Created: 2026-07-29T09:41:00Z
- Updated: 2026-08-11T09:00:50Z
- Closed: 2026-08-11T09:00:50Z

### Body

## Background

The VPTO backend currently provides PTODSL TileLib implementations for the
element-wise TileOps. Most implementations traverse a tile as a two-dimensional
region: an outer loop walks through rows and an inner vector loop processes the
columns of each row.

For a row-major tile whose valid region is physically contiguous, the same
operation can instead flatten the valid region and process it with a single
vector loop. This avoids per-row loop control and repeated row-tail handling.

The A5 implementation in [pto-isa](https://gitcode.com/cann/pto-isa.git)
already follows this model. For example,
[`TBinOp.hpp`](https://gitcode.com/cann/pto-isa/blob/master/include/pto/npu/a5/TBinOp.hpp)
contains separate 1D and 2D implementations and selects the applicable path
according to the tile shape and continuity conditions.

VPTO/PTODSL TileLib needs the same general capability. This issue is not only
about adding a 1D implementation for one binary operation. The goal is to make
**1D/2D template selection a common capability of all element-wise TileOps**.

## Scope

The scope covers all element-wise TileOps that currently have PTODSL TileLib
implementations for A5.

### Unary operations

- `tabs`
- `texp`
- `tlog`
- `tneg`
- `tnot`
- `trecip`
- `trelu`
- `trsqrt`
- `tsqrt`

### Tile-Tile operations

- `tadd`
- `tand`
- `tdiv`
- `tfmod`
- `tmax`
- `tmin`
- `tmul`
- `tor`
- `tprelu`
- `trem`
- `tshl`
- `tshr`
- `tsub`
- `txor`

### Tile-Scalar operations

- `tadds`
- `tands`
- `tdivs`
- `tfmods`
- `tlrelu`
- `tmaxs`
- `tmins`
- `tmuls`
- `tors`
- `trems`
- `tshls`
- `tshrs`
- `tsubs`
- `txors`

### Compare, select, conversion, and scalar fill operations

- `tcmp`
- `tcmps`
- `tsel`
- `tsels`
- `tcvt`
- `texpands`

The implementation may be delivered by operation family rather than in one
large change, but the common selection mechanism and the final acceptance must
cover the full list above. If an operation cannot legally use a flattened 1D
form because of its instruction semantics or data representation, that
exception must be documented and verified instead of silently omitted.

Reduction, row/column expansion, partial-update, load/store, data-movement,
sorting, random-number generation, and matrix operations are not part of this
issue. Although some of their implementations contain element-wise loops,
their TileOp semantics and layout requirements are different.

## Requirement

### 1. Provide reusable 1D and 2D element-wise template forms

PTODSL TileLib should provide reusable traversal forms for the major
element-wise families instead of implementing selection independently in every
operation:

- unary;
- Tile-Tile;
- Tile-Scalar;
- compare;
- select;
- conversion;
- scalar fill.

The 1D form flattens a legal valid region into one continuous element range and
uses one vector loop. The existing row-wise form remains the general 2D
fallback. Operation-specific computation, dtype restrictions, temporary
operands, masks, conversion modes, and scalar operand order must retain their
current semantics.

The template metadata must distinguish the two forms. In particular, the 1D
form should expose a one-dimensional loop structure and the 2D form should
retain its two-dimensional loop structure.

### 2. Define a common and conservative 1D legality rule

A 1D candidate may be selected only when every tile operand participating in
the traversal describes the same logical element range and that range can be
safely accessed as contiguous memory.

At a high level, the rule must consider:

- physical shape and valid shape;
- memory space;
- block layout and sub-layout;
- row stride or equivalent physical-continuity information;
- the shape and continuity of every input, output, mask, and temporary tile
  used by the operation;
- operation-specific restrictions such as predicate representation or
  source/destination dtype width changes.

For ordinary row-major tiles, a multi-row region is generally flattenable when
the valid column axis is full for every participating tile and there is no
padding or stride gap between adjacent rows. A single-row region may also be
flattenable. This should be encoded as an explicit shared constraint rather
than inferred only from an operation name or layout label.

Unknown or insufficient layout information must fall back to 2D. The 1D path
must never be selected speculatively.

Some element-wise operations need more specific rules:

- `tcmp`, `tcmps`, `tsel`, and `tsels` must account for predicate-mask layout
  and representation;
- `tcvt` must account for source/destination dtype widths and any packing or
  multi-step conversion form;
- operations carrying temporary Tile operands must include those operands in
  the legality decision;
- scalar operations must preserve normal and reverse operand forms where both
  are supported.

### 3. Make VPTO candidate selection deterministic

When both forms are legal, VPTO must select the 1D candidate. When the 1D
conditions are not met, VPTO must select the 2D candidate without changing the
TileOp result.

The complete selection path must preserve this decision:

```text
TileOp operand metadata
        -> PTODSL legality and ranking
        -> compact candidates attribute
        -> ExpandTileOp
        -> selected generated helper
```

Today the Python registry can rank candidates by priority, while the compiler
side stores and consumes a compact candidate list. The implementation must
ensure that priority/ordering is not lost between these stages and that the
expanded helper is the candidate selected by the legality and ranking rules.
Selection must not depend on Python import order, registration order, or an
accidental candidate ID order.

### 4. Keep specialization safe

All metadata that can change 1D legality or the generated helper body must be
available during candidate filtering and must participate in helper
specialization where applicable. Different shapes, valid shapes, layouts,
strides, memory spaces, operand forms, and conversion modes must not
incorrectly reuse the same generated helper.

### 5. Add family-level and end-to-end tests

Tests should demonstrate the common mechanism at the family level and ensure
that every operation in scope is registered with the expected 1D/2D behavior.
They do not need to duplicate every shape for every operation.

The test matrix should include, at minimum:

- contiguous multi-row full-axis input selecting 1D;
- contiguous single-row input selecting 1D;
- a multi-row tile with a non-full valid column axis selecting 2D;
- a stride gap, padding, or unsupported layout selecting 2D;
- vector-aligned and tail shapes;
- representative 8-bit, 16-bit, and 32-bit types supported by the operation
  families;
- representative unary, Tile-Tile, Tile-Scalar, compare, select, conversion,
  and scalar-fill operations;
- a catalog-level check proving that every operation listed in this issue has
  the required candidate coverage or an explicitly documented exception;
- VPTO expansion checks proving that the selected helper has the expected loop
  dimensionality;
- functional comparison showing identical results between legal 1D and 2D
  executions.

## Acceptance Criteria

The issue is complete when:

- all element-wise TileOps listed in the scope support deterministic 1D/2D
  selection, or have a reviewed and tested reason why a 1D form is not legal;
- eligible contiguous full-axis and single-row cases select a 1D helper;
- ineligible cases reliably retain the 2D helper;
- the 1D helper uses one flattened vector traversal rather than a row loop plus
  a column loop;
- tail processing is correct and neither path reads or writes outside the
  logical valid region;
- candidate selection remains consistent from PTODSL legality analysis through
  `ExpandTileOp`;
- selection is independent of template registration/import order;
- 1D and 2D executions produce equivalent results for the supported dtype and
  shape combinations;
- existing VPTO element-wise tests continue to pass;
- focused metadata-selection, expansion, functional, and performance tests are
  added;
- the shared legality and selection rules are documented for future
  element-wise TileOps.

## Performance Goal

Performance is evaluated by comparing the new 1D candidate with the existing
2D candidate for the **same TileOp, dtype, logical shape, data, compiler
options, and execution environment**. Comparison with another repository's
implementation is not required.

The expected direction is:

- the 1D path removes the outer row loop and its loop-control overhead;
- it avoids restarting vector traversal and tail state for every row;
- it does not add layout conversion, temporary-buffer movement, or extra
  vector computation;
- its vector compute instruction count is consistent with processing the
  flattened valid element count;
- it provides a measurable benefit for contiguous multi-row shapes where the
  row dimension creates meaningful 2D loop overhead;
- it is not slower than the 2D candidate for the selected benchmark set.

The performance report should cover representative operations from each major
family rather than only one operation. It should include multiple dtypes,
single-row and multi-row shapes, vector-aligned and tail shapes, and both 1D
eligible and 2D fallback layouts.

For each case, report at least:

- operation, dtype, physical shape, and valid shape;
- selected candidate and loop dimensionality;
- 1D and 2D execution cycles or latency under the same environment;
- relative improvement of 1D over 2D;
- confirmation that functional results are identical.

The optimization should demonstrate a stable overall benefit on 1D-eligible
element-wise workloads, with no material regression in cases that continue to
use the 2D fallback. Exact per-operation thresholds may be determined from the
benchmark baseline because different element-wise instructions have different
compute costs.

## Relevant Code Areas

- `ptodsl/ptodsl/tilelib/templates/a5/_elementwise.py`
- `ptodsl/ptodsl/tilelib/templates/a5/_remainder.py`
- the operation-specific A5 templates under
  `ptodsl/ptodsl/tilelib/templates/a5/`
- `ptodsl/ptodsl/tilelib/constraints.py`
- `ptodsl/ptodsl/tilelib/registry.py`
- `ptodsl/ptodsl/tilelib/serving/daemon.py`
- `lib/PTO/Transforms/InsertTemplateAttributes.cpp`
- `lib/PTO/Transforms/ExpandTileOp.cpp`
- PTODSL TileLib selection/render tests and VPTO lit tests



---

## #1052 [Bug] PTODSL's `ast_rewrite` reports incorrect traceback line numbers

- State: open
- URL: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/PTOAS/issues/1052
- Created: 2026-07-29T15:12:36Z
- Updated: 2026-07-29T15:15:48Z
- Closed: 

### Body

### Component

PTODSL

### Description

PTODSL `@pto.jit` 的 `ast_rewrite` 默认开启，启用后，若编译期间在函数内发生异常，调用栈显示的行号可能是函数源码片段的相对行号，而不是它在文件中的实际行号

这会让报错指向完全无关的代码，增加定位难度


### Reproduction (minimal)

```python
# Copyright (c) 2026 Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd.
# This program is free software, you can redistribute it and/or modify it under the terms and conditions of
# CANN Open Software License Agreement Version 2.0 (the "License").
# Please refer to the License for details. You may not use this file except in compliance with the License.
# THIS SOFTWARE IS PROVIDED ON AN "AS IS" BASIS, WITHOUT WARRANTIES OF ANY KIND, EITHER EXPRESS OR IMPLIED,
# INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO NON-INFRINGEMENT, MERCHANTABILITY, OR FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.
# See LICENSE in the root of the software repository for the full text of the License.

from ptodsl import pto


@pto.jit(target="a5")
def ast_rewrite_traceback():
    runtime_value = pto.const(1, dtype=pto.i32)
    _ = not runtime_value  # 实际出错位置


ast_rewrite_traceback.compile()
```

### Expected behavior

编译报错后，调用栈中显示实际报错位置

```python
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "ast_rewrite_traceback.py", line 18, in <module>
    ast_rewrite_traceback.compile()
  File "ptodsl/ptodsl/_jit.py", line 290, in compile
    return self._compiler.compile(**constexpr_bindings)
  File "ptodsl/ptodsl/_kernel_compilation.py", line 138, in compile
    compiled.build()
  File "ptodsl/ptodsl/_tracing/artifacts.py", line 34, in build
    built = self._module_factory()
  File "ptodsl/ptodsl/_tracing/runtime.py", line 86, in build_module
    self.trace_entry(*args)
  File "ptodsl/ptodsl/_tracing/runtime.py", line 128, in trace_entry
    result = self._callback(*args, **kwargs)
  File "ast_rewrite_traceback.py", line 15, in ast_rewrite_traceback
    _ = not runtime_value  # 实际出错位置
  File "ptodsl/ptodsl/_surface_values.py", line 239, in __bool__
    raise native_python_control_flow_error("if/while condition")
ptodsl._diagnostics.PTODSLTracingMisuseError: native Python if/while condition cannot consume a PTODSL runtime value during tracing. This value is a device-side SSA/runtime-metadata value, not a Python bool/int. Use pto.if_(...) or pto.for_(...) for device-side control flow, or keep the bound/condition in pto.const_expr.
```

### Actual behavior / error logs

编译报错后，调用栈中显示错误的位置和行号

```python
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "ast_rewrite_traceback.py", line 18, in <module>
    ast_rewrite_traceback.compile()
  File "ptodsl/ptodsl/_jit.py", line 290, in compile
    return self._compiler.compile(**constexpr_bindings)
  File "ptodsl/ptodsl/_kernel_compilation.py", line 138, in compile
    compiled.build()
  File "ptodsl/ptodsl/_tracing/artifacts.py", line 34, in build
    built = self._module_factory()
  File "ptodsl/ptodsl/_tracing/runtime.py", line 86, in build_module
    self.trace_entry(*args)
  File "ptodsl/ptodsl/_tracing/runtime.py", line 128, in trace_entry
    result = self._callback(*args, **kwargs)
  File "ast_rewrite_traceback.py", line 4, in ast_rewrite_traceback
    # Please refer to the License for details. You may not use this file except in compliance with the License.
  File "ptodsl/ptodsl/_surface_values.py", line 239, in __bool__
    raise native_python_control_flow_error("if/while condition")
ptodsl._diagnostics.PTODSLTracingMisuseError: native Python if/while condition cannot consume a PTODSL runtime value during tracing. This value is a device-side SSA/runtime-metadata value, not a Python bool/int. Use pto.if_(...) or pto.for_(...) for device-side control flow, or keep the bound/condition in pto.const_expr.
```

若手动关闭 `ast_rewrite`： `@pto.jit(target="a5", ast_rewrite=False)`，则可获得期望结果

## #1058 [Feature] Validate VMI register types in PTODSL and TileLang frontends

- State: closed
- URL: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/PTOAS/issues/1058
- Created: 2026-07-30T01:04:03Z
- Updated: 2026-08-05T07:06:37Z
- Closed: 2026-08-05T07:06:37Z

### Body

### Summary

Add frontend validation for VMI register types in both PTODSL and TileLang. Invalid VMI register element types should be rejected before generating or lowering PTO/VMI IR, instead of failing later in an MLIR verifier, lowering, code generation, or compilation.

### Motivation / use case

PTODSL and TileLang users can currently construct VMI programs with register types that are not legal for VMI. The error is discovered too late, so diagnostics are farther from the source declaration and may surface as a confusing backend failure.

Both frontends should provide the same early and actionable validation behavior. This also prevents PTODSL and TileLang from accepting different type sets for equivalent VMI programs.

### Proposed API / behavior

- Define or reuse a single source of truth for the VMI register element types supported by PTOAS, including integer signedness/width, floating-point and low-precision types as applicable.
- Validate VMI register types when PTODSL and TileLang construct or compile VMI values/operations, before IR lowering or code generation.
- Reject an unsupported type with a frontend diagnostic that identifies the offending register/value, the supplied type, and the expected legal type set.
- Apply the validation consistently to explicit register declarations and inferred/result register types.
- Keep the existing IR/backend verifier checks as a defensive fallback.
- Do not change the behavior of programs that use legal VMI register types.

### Acceptance criteria

- PTODSL rejects an illegal VMI register type at frontend compile time with an actionable diagnostic.
- TileLang rejects the equivalent illegal type at frontend compile time with an equivalent diagnostic.
- Focused negative tests cover illegal explicit and inferred/result types in both frontends.
- Positive tests confirm representative legal integer, floating-point, and supported low-precision VMI register types remain accepted.
- The legal type definition is shared or otherwise kept centralized so the two frontends cannot silently drift.

### Alternatives considered

Relying only on the existing VMI IR verifier or downstream compiler errors preserves correctness, but reports the problem too late and produces a worse frontend user experience.

## #1059 [Bug] `pto.for_` 循环携带的 vreg 累加器在 `pto.if_` 嵌套 region 中未正确 yield，导致 MLIR 支配关系错误

- State: closed
- URL: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/PTOAS/issues/1059
- Created: 2026-07-30T01:58:15Z
- Updated: 2026-08-01T10:06:37Z
- Closed: 2026-08-01T10:06:37Z

### Body

### Component

EmitC / Codegen (lib/PTO/Transforms/PTOToEmitC.cpp)

### Description

在 ptodsl 中，当一个 vreg 累加器在 `pto.if_` 的 then 分支内通过 `pto.for_` 循环累加（`acc = pto.vadd(acc, ...)`），并在循环结束后被 `pto.vsts` 使用时，ptodsl tracing 未将该累加器纳入 `scf.for` 的 `iter_args`/`yield` 链，导致 MLIR 验证报支配关系错误：

```
error: operand #0 does not dominate this use
note: see current operation: "pto.vsts"(%17, %13, %14, %2) <{dist = "NORM_B32"}> : (!pto.vreg<64xf32>, !pto.ptr<f32, ub>, index, !pto.mask<b32>) -> ()
note: operand defined here (op in a child region)
```

### Reproduction (minimal)

```markdown
from ptodsl import pto, scalar

@pto.jit(name="repro_dominance_vreg_acc", target="a5", kernel_kind="vector", mode="explicit")
def kernel(buf: pto.ptr(pto.f32, "gm")):
    ub = pto.castptr(pto.const(0, dtype=pto.i64), pto.ptr(pto.i8, "ub"))
    mask = pto.pset_b32("PAT_ALL")

    # 初始化累加器
    acc = pto.vdup(pto.const(0.0, dtype=pto.f32), mask)

    cond = pto.const(1, dtype=pto.i32) != 0
    with pto.if_(cond) as br, br.then_:
        with pto.for_(0, 4, step=1) as i:
            x = pto.vdup(pto.const(1.0, dtype=pto.f32), mask)
            acc = pto.vadd(acc, x, mask)

        # 循环后使用 acc —— 支配关系错误
        pto.vsts(
            acc,
            pto.addptr(pto.castptr(ub, pto.ptr(pto.f32, "ub")), 0),
            pto.const(0),
            mask,
            dist="NORM_B32",
        )

mlir = kernel.compile().mlir_text()
print(mlir)
```

### Expected behavior

`scf.for` 的 `iter_args` 应包含 `acc` 对应的 vreg，循环后 `pto.vsts` 引用 yield 结果，满足 SSA 支配关系。

### Actual behavior / error logs

```text
mlir._mlir_libs._site_initialize.<locals>.MLIRError: Verification failed:
error: unknown: operand #0 does not dominate this use
note: unknown: see current operation: "pto.vsts"(%17, %13, %14, %2) <{dist = "NORM_B32"}> : (!pto.vreg<64xf32>, !pto.ptr<f32, ub>, index, !pto.mask<b32>) -> ()
note: unknown: operand defined here (op in a child region)


`scf.for` 的 `iter_args` 未包含 `acc`，累加器 vreg 的定义被限制在循环体 region 内，循环后的 `pto.vsts` 引用了不支配的操作数。
```

## #1060 [Bug] MXFP4 L1 到 L0 展开生成了错误的非零 K 偏移和 scale stride【阻塞】

- State: closed
- URL: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/PTOAS/issues/1060
- Created: 2026-07-30T02:41:12Z
- Updated: 2026-08-13T03:28:03Z
- Closed: 2026-08-13T03:28:03Z

### Body

### Component

PTO Dialect / ODS (include/PTO/IR)

### Description

## 问题描述

在将 MXFP4 L1→L0 wrapper 操作展开为 VPTO 底层操作时，存在两个控制参数无法正确表达的问题：

1. packed FP4 数据加载的非零 `start_col` 被额外除以 2。例如，`start_col = 4` 最终被展开为 `k_start = 2`。
2. MX scale 加载的源 stride 和目标 stride 只能根据逻辑 tile shape 自动推导。对于需要 `src_stride = 8`、`dst_stride = 4` 的合法 scale 布局，当前会展开为 `4, 4`，并且 wrapper 操作没有提供显式指定 stride 的方式。

这两个问题会导致第二个 K 子块与第一个 K 子块发生数据重叠，或者从错误的 L1 位置加载 scale metadata，最终产生静默数值错误。

## 影响范围

该问题会影响以下 MXFP4 kernel：

- K 维被拆分为多个 L1→L0 子块；
- MX scale 在 L1 中的物理 source stride 与自动推导值不同。

生成的 kernel 可以正常编译和运行，不会报告地址或类型错误，但可能读取重叠的数据或错误的 scale metadata，最终产生静默数值错误。


### Reproduction (minimal)

```markdown
## 完整最小复现

将以下内容保存为 `repro_mxfp4_l1_l0.pto`：


module attributes {
  pto.target_arch = "a5",
  pto.kernel_kind = #pto.kernel_kind<cube>
} {
  func.func @repro(
      %data: !pto.ptr<!pto.f4E2M1x2, l1>,
      %scale: !pto.ptr<!pto.f4E2M1x2, l1>,
      %dst: !pto.ptr<!pto.f4E2M1x2, l0a>)
      attributes {pto.kernel} {
    %c0 = arith.constant 0 : i64
    %c4 = arith.constant 4 : i64
    %c256 = arith.constant 256 : i64

    // 加载第二个逻辑 K=256 的 MXFP4 子块。
    pto.mte_l1_l0a
        %data, %dst, %c256, %c256, %c0, %c4
        : !pto.ptr<!pto.f4E2M1x2, l1>,
          !pto.ptr<!pto.f4E2M1x2, l0a>,
          i64, i64, i64, i64

    // scale 在 L1 中的 NZ 源 stride 为 8，
    // 在 L0 中的目标 stride 为 4。
    // 当前 wrapper 没有参数可以表达这两个物理布局 stride。
    pto.mte_l1_l0a_mx
        %scale, %dst, %c256, %c256, %c0, %c0
        : !pto.ptr<!pto.f4E2M1x2, l1>,
          !pto.ptr<!pto.f4E2M1x2, l0a>,
          i64, i64, i64, i64

    return
  }
}


执行以下命令：


ptoas \
  --pto-arch=a5 \
  --pto-backend=vpto \
  --emit-vpto \
  repro_mxfp4_l1_l0.pto \
  -o repro_mxfp4_l1_l0.vpto

grep -E "load_cbuf_to_ca_(s4|mx)" repro_mxfp4_l1_l0.vpto
```

### Expected behavior

## 期望行为

生成的控制参数应等价于：

```mlir
pto.load_cbuf_to_ca_s4 ..., 0, 4, 16, 4, 16, 16, 0
pto.load_cbuf_to_ca_mx ..., 0, 0, 16, 4, 8, 4
```

对于 packed FP4：

- 表示加载长度的 `k_step` 可以根据 packed 数据宽度进行换算；
- 已经由调用方提供的 `k_start` 控制坐标应保持为 `4`，不应再次除以 2。

MX scale wrapper 还应允许调用方显式提供 source stride 和 destination stride。当调用方没有提供时，可以继续使用现有的自动推导逻辑，以保持向后兼容。


### Actual behavior / error logs

```text
## 实际行为

生成的底层操作等价于：


// m_start, k_start, m_step, k_step,
// src_stride, dst_stride, transpose
pto.load_cbuf_to_ca_s4 ..., 0, 2, 16, 4, 16, 16, 0

// x_start, y_start, x_step, y_step,
// src_stride, dst_stride
pto.load_cbuf_to_ca_mx ..., 0, 0, 16, 4, 4, 4


存在以下问题：

- 数据加载中传入的 `start_col = 4` 被展开为 `k_start = 2`。
- scale 加载自动推导出 `src_stride = 4`，但实际布局要求为 `8`。
- 当前 wrapper 没有提供显式指定 scale source/destination stride 的参数。
```

## #1061 [Bug] Soft SYNCALL EmitC uses the removed PTO-ISA UB/L1 ABI

- State: closed
- URL: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/PTOAS/issues/1061
- Created: 2026-07-30T03:14:11Z
- Updated: 2026-08-01T11:33:51Z
- Closed: 2026-08-01T11:33:51Z

### Body

## Problem

PTO-ISA commit [`f24f7b736b689cc107b9eb2d362be6a7718fcc99`](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pto-isa/commit/f24f7b736b689cc107b9eb2d362be6a7718fcc99) changed soft `SYNCALL` for AIV-only, AIC-only, and Mix to one unified public API:

```cpp
SYNCALL<SyncAllMode::Soft, CoreType>(gmWorkspace, usedCores);
```

UB/L1 scratch arguments were removed. The GM workspace now reserves one exclusive 64-byte cache line: at least 16 `int32_t` elements, zero-initialized before first use.

Current PTOAS `main` still models and emits the old ABI:

- AIV-only: `gm_workspace + ub_workspace [+ used_cores]`
- AIC-only: `gm_workspace + l1_workspace [+ used_cores]`
- Mix: `gm_workspace + ub_workspace + l1_workspace [+ used_cores]`

References at `main@68df7d3a`:

- [`SyncAllOp`](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/PTOAS/blob/68df7d3a4347bcbe7932088b7a2ec48c584cd800/include/PTO/IR/PTOOps.td#L3153-L3182)
- [`PTOSyncAllToEmitC`](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/PTOAS/blob/68df7d3a4347bcbe7932088b7a2ec48c584cd800/lib/PTO/Transforms/PTOToEmitC.cpp#L6097-L6208)

The generated 3/4-argument C++ calls do not compile with PTO-ISA f24 or its descendants. This blocks PyPTO from moving its runtime/PTO-ISA pin forward while retaining generic soft `pl.system.syncall`.

## Required changes

1. Change the soft `SyncAllOp` operand ABI to `gm_workspace` plus optional `used_cores`. Remove `ub_workspace` and `l1_workspace`. Keep hard mode as a zero-operand op.
2. Update the custom parser, printer, verifier, ODS-generated bindings, and documentation. Soft mode must require an i32 GM workspace with static capacity of at least 16 elements. Optional `used_cores` must be i32.
3. Update `PTOSyncAllToEmitC` so every soft core type emits exactly `SYNCALL<SyncAllMode::Soft, CoreType>(gmWorkspace, usedCores)`. If `used_cores` is omitted, materialize `int32_t{0}`. Remove the UB/L1 switch and `buildSyncAllWorkspaceTileValue` path.
4. Add AIV-only, AIC-only, Mix, omitted-used, and hard-mode regression tests. Compile the generated C++ against PTO-ISA f24 or an explicit descendant SHA.

## Expected IR and C++

```mlir
pto.syncall(%gm, %used : !pto.partition_tensor_view<16xi32>, i32)
  mode = #pto.sync_all_mode<soft>,
  core_type = #pto.sync_core_type<aiv_only>
```

```cpp
SYNCALL<SyncAllMode::Soft, SyncCoreType::AIVOnly>(gmWorkspace, usedCores);
```

The same two-argument C++ shape is required for `AICOnly` and `Mix`.

## Acceptance criteria

- AIV-only, AIC-only, and Mix EmitC calls have exactly two arguments.
- No soft-SYNCALL UB/L1 Tile, `TASSIGN`, or local scratch is generated.
- Missing `used_cores` lowers to `int32_t{0}`.
- GM workspace smaller than 16 `int32_t` elements is rejected when its static size is known.
- Hard SYNCALL behavior is unchanged.

## Compatibility option

If an atomic producer upgrade is not possible, one transition release may accept both the old and new PTO IR forms. Legacy UB/L1 operands must be deprecated and ignored, and EmitC must always generate the new two-argument PTO-ISA call. Please provide the merged commit SHA and a release tag/wheel that PyPTO can pin.

---

## #1067 [Feature] 放宽向量掩码粒度验证，允许 mask 粒度宽于输入向量元素粒度

- State: closed
- URL: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/PTOAS/issues/1067
- Created: 2026-07-30T09:30:16Z
- Updated: 2026-07-30T10:02:38Z
- Closed: 2026-07-30T10:02:38Z

### Body

### Summary

## 问题描述

当向量操作的输入向量经过类型转换（如 `vcvt`）后元素位宽发生变化（如 32-bit 元素变为 16-bit 元素，元素数量从 64 变为 128），用户传入的 mask 粒度与转换后的向量元素粒度不匹配，VPTO 验证报错。

## 复现场景

先用 `vcvt` 把 64 个 int32（256 字节）转换为 128 个 int16（256 字节），再用 `vcadd` 对 int16 向量做相邻配对求和。mask 是在 `vcvt` 之前用 `vcmp` 对 int32 向量比较生成的，粒度为 `mask<b32>`：

```
%mask = pto.vcmp ... : ... -> !pto.mask<b32>
%vec16 = pto.vcvt %vec32, %mask, ... : !pto.vreg<64xi32>, !pto.mask<b32> -> !pto.vreg<128xi16>
%result = pto.vcadd %vec16, %mask : !pto.vreg<128xi16>, !pto.mask<b32> -> !pto.vreg<64xi32>
```

`vcadd` 收到的 mask 是 `mask<b32>`，而 128 个 int16 元素期望的是 `mask<b16>`，VPTO 报错：

```
'pto.vcadd' op mask type '!pto.mask<b32>' does not match input vector type '!pto.vreg<128xi16>'; expected !pto.mask<b16>
```

## 根因分析

### CANN 硬件的 mask 机制

CANN 硬件的掩码寄存器是 **256 个 bit**，每个 bit 对应 1 字节数据。元素宽度只决定"几个 bit 控制一个元素"：

| 元素位宽 | 元素数量 | 每 1 个元素对应的 mask bit 数 |
|---------|---------|---------------------------|
| 4 字节（int32/float32） | 64 个 | 4 个 bit |
| 2 字节（int16/float16） | 128 个 | 2 个 bit |
| 1 字节（int8） | 256 个 | 1 个 bit |

当元素从 int32 变成 int16 时，原来控制 4 字节（1 个 int32）的 4 个 bit，变成控制 2 组各 2 字节（2 个 int16）。**256 个 bit 始终覆盖全部 256 字节，按不同元素宽度自然分组，不需要转换。**

CANN 的 `vector_bool` 类型就是一个 256-bit 的整体，不区分粒度。同一个 `vector_bool` 传给操作 int32 的指令和操作 int16 的指令都行——**硬件根据当前指令的操作数类型自动解释掩码粒度**。

### PTODSL 的类型系统限制

PTODSL 把掩码粒度显式编码到类型系统里：`mask<b8>`、`mask<b16>`、`mask<b32>`。虽然底层都是 256 个 bit（`VectorType::get({256}, i1)`），但类型系统认为它们是不同的类型，要求 mask 粒度必须和向量元素位宽**严格匹配**。

当 `vcvt` 把向量从 `int32x64` 变成 `int16x128` 时，对应的 mask 应该从 `b32` 变为 `b16`——把每个 bit "分裂"成 2 个相同的 bit。这个操作在硬件上是自然的（256 bit 按元素宽度重新分组），但 PTODSL 的类型系统无法表达这种转换。

## 建议方案：放宽 mask 粒度验证

在 VPTO 的 mask 粒度验证中（`PTOValidateVPTOIR.cpp` 的 `validateMaskMatchesVectorFamily`），允许 mask 粒度**宽于**输入向量的元素粒度。具体来说：

- mask 粒度为 `b32`，输入向量元素为 16-bit 时，不报错，自动按 16-bit 粒度解释 mask
- mask 粒度为 `b32`，输入向量元素为 8-bit 时，同理
- mask 粒度为 `b16`，输入向量元素为 8-bit 时，同理

这与 CANN 硬件的行为一致——256 bit 的 mask 就在那里，硬件根据当前指令的操作数类型自动选择粒度，不需要类型系统强制匹配。

### 为什么这个方案合理

1. **与硬件行为一致**：CANN 硬件的 `vector_bool` 本来就不区分粒度，同一个掩码寄存器传给不同元素宽度的指令时，硬件自动按操作数类型解释
2. **语义明确**：mask 粒度宽于向量元素粒度时，每个 mask bit 自然覆盖多个连续的细粒度元素，这些元素要么全部激活要么全部不激活，语义等价于窄粒度 mask
3. **mask 粒度窄于向量元素粒度的场景仍应报错**：例如 `mask<b8>` 给 `int32x64` 用是不合法的，因为 8-bit 粒度的 mask 无法精确控制 32-bit 元素的对齐边界——这种方向的不匹配仍然需要验证

### 对现有代码的影响

放宽验证不会影响已有的 mask 粒度匹配的场景（mask 粒度 == 向量元素粒度时行为不变）。只影响 mask 粒度**宽于**向量元素粒度的场景。

## 涉及的代码

- `lib/PTO/Transforms/PTOValidateVPTOIR.cpp` 的 `validateMaskMatchesVectorFamily` 函数
- `lib/PTO/IR/VPTO.cpp` 中 `VcvtOp::verify` 的 mask 粒度检查

### Motivation / use case

-

### Proposed API / behavior

_No response_

### Alternatives considered

_No response_

### Additional context

## #1069 [Bug] pto.comm.tput/tget verifier rejects dynamic partition-view shapes that the rest of the pipeline already lowers

- State: closed
- URL: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/PTOAS/issues/1069
- Created: 2026-07-30T11:01:15Z
- Updated: 2026-08-03T01:09:17Z
- Closed: 2026-08-03T01:09:17Z

### Body

### Component

Verifier / IR semantics (lib/PTO/IR)

### Description

`verifyCommGlobalLike()` rejects any `?` (dynamic) dimension on the `dst`/`src` partition views of `pto.comm.tput` and `pto.comm.tget`, so a variable-size transfer cannot be expressed — even though **the rest of the pipeline already handles it end to end**.

The verifier is the *only* blocker. I confirmed this by bypassing it (see "Proof the lowering already works" below): with the check out of the way, a fully `?`-dimensioned `pto.comm.tput` lowers cleanly to a runtime-extent `GlobalTensor` and a valid `pto::comm::TPUT(...)` call, on both v0.48 and v0.54.

Why the rejection looks unintentional rather than a real constraint:

1. **`pto.partition_view` with a `?` result type + dynamic size SSA already lowers fine** — it just isn't allowed to reach a comm op. The same partition view feeding `pto.tload` compiles without complaint (case C below).
2. **The live lowering path is dynamic-capable.** `pto.partition_view` → (`PTOViewToMemref.cpp:1330` `lowerPartitionViewOps`) → `memref.subview` with dynamic sizes → `SubviewToEmitCPattern` (`PTOToEmitC.cpp:3766`), which passes `adaptor.getSizes()` straight into the `pto::Shape` constructor (`PTOToEmitC.cpp:4172-4184`). The static-only early-return in `buildGlobalTensorFromMemref` (`PTOToEmitC.cpp:4406`) sits on the *memref-direct* path, which comm ops built from partition views never take.
3. **`GlobalTensor` can express runtime extents.** `pto::DYNAMIC = -1` and `pto::Shape` / `pto::Stride` have runtime constructors (pto-isa `include/pto/common/pto_tile.hpp`), which is exactly what `SubviewToEmitCPattern` emits.
4. **pto-isa reads the shape at runtime.** `TPUT_IMPL` (pto-isa `include/pto/comm/a2a3/TPut.hpp`) obtains extents via `srcGlobalData.GetShape(GlobalTensorDim::DIM_n)`, with no shape-related `static_assert`; the 2-D slide auto-chunks a transfer larger than the staging tile.

Impact: push-based collectives in pypto must transfer the full compile-time capacity instead of the actual runtime count. In `all_to_all_v` / MoE dispatch, a peer that receives 1 of 32 possible rows still costs 32 rows of interconnect bandwidth. pypto codegen already emits the dynamic form (`!pto.partition_tensor_view<?x64xf16>` with a static chunked staging tile), so it fails at the ptoas verifier today — see pypto issue [#2213](https://github.com/hw-native-sys/pypto/issues/2213).

### Reproduction (minimal)

**Case A — dynamic `pto.comm.tput` (fails).** Identical to the static version except `sizes` uses a runtime `%rows` and the partition-view type is `<?x4096xi8>`:

```mlir
module attributes {pto.target_arch = "a2a3"} {
  func.func @tput_dynamic(%arg0: !pto.ptr<i8>, %arg1: !pto.ptr<i8>, %arg2: i32,
                          %__pypto_spmd_block_idx: i32, %__pypto_spmd_block_num: i32)
      attributes {pto.kernel_kind = #pto.kernel_kind<vector>} {
    %c0_i64 = arith.constant 0 : i64
    %c0_index = arith.constant 0 : index
    %c1_index = arith.constant 1 : index
    %c32_index = arith.constant 32 : index
    %c4096_index = arith.constant 4096 : index
    %rows = arith.index_cast %arg2 : i32 to index
    %dst_view = pto.make_tensor_view %arg0, shape = [%c32_index, %c4096_index], strides = [%c4096_index, %c1_index] {layout = #pto.layout<nd>}: !pto.tensor_view<?x?xi8>
    %src_view = pto.make_tensor_view %arg1, shape = [%c32_index, %c4096_index], strides = [%c4096_index, %c1_index] {layout = #pto.layout<nd>}: !pto.tensor_view<?x?xi8>
    %stage = pto.alloc_tile addr = %c0_i64 valid_row = %c1_index valid_col = %c4096_index : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=i8, rows=1, cols=4096, v_row=?, v_col=?, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>
    %dst_pview = pto.partition_view %dst_view, offsets = [%c0_index, %c0_index], sizes = [%rows, %c4096_index] : !pto.tensor_view<?x?xi8> -> !pto.partition_tensor_view<?x4096xi8>
    %src_pview = pto.partition_view %src_view, offsets = [%c0_index, %c0_index], sizes = [%rows, %c4096_index] : !pto.tensor_view<?x?xi8> -> !pto.partition_tensor_view<?x4096xi8>
    pto.barrier <PIPE_ALL>
    pto.comm.tput(%dst_pview, %src_pview, buf(%stage) : !pto.partition_tensor_view<?x4096xi8>, !pto.partition_tensor_view<?x4096xi8>, !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=i8, rows=1, cols=4096, v_row=?, v_col=?, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>) {atomicType = #pto<atomic_type atomic_none>}
    pto.barrier <PIPE_ALL>
    return
  }
}
```

```bash
ptoas dynamic.pto -o dynamic.cpp --pto-level=level3
# same file with sizes = [%c32_index, ...] and <32x4096xi8> succeeds
```

**Case B — same file with `pto.comm.tget`**: same error (`'pto.comm.tget' op expects dst to have a positive static shape`).

**Case C — the same dynamic partition view feeding `pto.tload` (succeeds).** Shows the `?` partition view itself is fine; only the comm ops reject it:

```mlir
    %pv = pto.partition_view %view, offsets = [%c0_index, %c0_index], sizes = [%rows, %c32_index] : !pto.tensor_view<?x?xf32> -> !pto.partition_tensor_view<?x32xf32>
    pto.tload ins(%pv : !pto.partition_tensor_view<?x32xf32>) outs(%tb : !pto.tile_buf<loc=vec, dtype=f32, rows=1, cols=32, v_row=?, v_col=?, blayout=row_major, slayout=none_box, fractal=512, pad=0>)
```

emits the runtime extent and `TLOAD` without error:

```cpp
pto::Shape<1, 1, 1, -1, 32> v10 = pto::Shape<1, 1, 1, -1, 32>(v8);
GlobalTensor<float, pto::Shape<1, 1, 1, -1, 32>, pto::Stride<-1, -1, -1, 32, 1>, pto::Layout::ND> v12 = ...;
TLOAD(v13, v12);
```

**Proof the lowering already works.** Taking Case A and only routing the staging tile through `pto.bind_tile` (so `shouldBypassDecodedMemrefVerifier`, `PTO.cpp:514`, skips the check) makes the *same* `?x4096` tput lower successfully on both v0.48 and v0.54:

```mlir
    %ubuf = memref.alloc() : memref<1x4096xi8, #pto.address_space<vec>>
    %stage = pto.bind_tile %ubuf, %c1_index, %c4096_index
      {config = #pto.tile_buf_config<blayout=0 : i32, slayout=0 : i32, s_fractal_size=512, pad=0 : i32>}
      : memref<1x4096xi8, #pto.address_space<vec>> -> memref<1x4096xi8, #pto.address_space<vec>>
    pto.comm.tput(%dst_pview, %src_pview, buf(%stage) : !pto.partition_tensor_view<?x4096xi8>, !pto.partition_tensor_view<?x4096xi8>, memref<1x4096xi8, #pto.address_space<vec>>) {atomicType = #pto<atomic_type atomic_none>}
```

```bash
$ ptoas dyn_bypass.pto -o dyn_bypass.cpp --pto-level=level2   # exit 0, no diagnostics
```

```cpp
pto::Shape<1, 1, 1, -1, 4096> v11 = pto::Shape<1, 1, 1, -1, 4096>(v9);            // v9 = runtime rows
pto::Stride<-1, -1, -1, 4096, 1> v12 = pto::Stride<-1, -1, -1, 4096, 1>(v10, v10, v10);
GlobalTensor<int8_t, pto::Shape<1, 1, 1, -1, 4096>, pto::Stride<-1, -1, -1, 4096, 1>, pto::Layout::ND> v13 = ...;
pto::comm::TPUT(v13, v17, v19);
```

`--emit-pto-ir` on that run confirms the intermediate form the EmitC patterns consume — a dynamic `memref.subview`, with the comm op already memref-typed at that point:

```mlir
%subview = memref.subview %reinterpret_cast[0, 0] [%0, 4096] [1, 1] {layout = #pto.layout<nd>} : memref<?x?xi8, strided<[?, ?], offset: ?>, #pto.address_space<gm>> to memref<?x4096xi8, strided<[?, ?], offset: ?>, #pto.address_space<gm>>
pto.comm.tput(%subview, %subview_1, buf(%2) : memref<?x4096xi8, strided<[?, ?], offset: ?>, #pto.address_space<gm>>, ...)
```

### Expected behavior

`pto.comm.tput` / `pto.comm.tget` should accept `?` dimensions on their `dst`/`src` partition views and lower them to a runtime-extent `GlobalTensor`, exactly as Case C and the bypass run already do — the number of rows on the wire then equals the runtime payload instead of the compile-time capacity.

Suggested fix in `verifyCommGlobalLike` (`lib/PTO/IR/PTO.cpp:4187-4191`): keep rejecting non-positive *static* dims, allow `kDynamic`:

```cpp
for (int64_t dim : shape) {
  if (dim != ShapedType::kDynamic && dim <= 0)
    return op->emitOpError() << "expects " << name
                             << " to have a positive or dynamic shape";
}
```

Two related spots to consider in the same review:

- `TPutOp::verify()` / `TGetOp::verify()` (`PTO.cpp:16844` / `:16862`) compare `getShapeVec(dst) != getShapeVec(src)` under the message "same static shape". With `?` allowed, two dynamic extents comparing equal as `kDynamic` is the right structural check, but the diagnostic wording should be updated.
- `verifyCommSignalLike` and `verifyCommStagingTileLike` (`PTO.cpp:4195` / `:4206`) reuse the same positive-static loop. Signals and VEC staging tiles genuinely want static shapes, so please keep those strict — only the GM `dst`/`src` views of tput/tget need relaxing.

### Actual behavior / error logs

```text
$ ptoas dynamic.pto -o dynamic.cpp --pto-level=level3
loc("dynamic.pto":17:5): error: 'pto.comm.tput' op expects dst to have a positive static shape
Error: Failed to parse MLIR.

$ ptoas dyn_tget.pto -o dyn_tget.cpp --pto-level=level3
loc("dyn_tget.pto":17:5): error: 'pto.comm.tget' op expects dst to have a positive static shape
Error: Failed to parse MLIR.
```

Reproduced identically on released binaries **v0.48, v0.50 and v0.54**, and with real pypto codegen output (`pld.tensor.put(..., shape=[n, 64], chunk_rows=4, chunk_cols=32)`):

```text
loc("pypto_dyn_put.pto":22:3): error: 'pto.comm.tput' op expects dst to have a positive static shape
Error: Failed to parse MLIR.
```

Origin (v0.54, `lib/PTO/IR/PTO.cpp:4177-4192`):

```cpp
static LogicalResult verifyCommGlobalLike(Operation *op, Value value,
                                          StringRef name) {
  ...
  for (int64_t dim : shape) {
    if (dim == ShapedType::kDynamic || dim <= 0)
      return op->emitOpError() << "expects " << name
                               << " to have a positive static shape";
  }
  return success();
}
```

## #1073 [Bug] [阻塞] PTODSL: variable reassignment inside pto.if_ is not carried out correctly and may cause dominance errors

- State: closed
- URL: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/PTOAS/issues/1073
- Created: 2026-07-30T13:10:50Z
- Updated: 2026-08-03T02:58:14Z
- Closed: 2026-08-03T02:58:14Z

### Body

### Component

Python bindings (python/)

### Description

PTODSL 中，如果一个变量在 `pto.if_` 的 then/else region 内被重新赋值，并且这个变量在 `pto.if_` 之后继续使用，目前看起来没有被正确 lower 成 `scf.if` 的 result/yield。

这会导致两类问题：

1. 简单赋值可能被错误地当成无条件赋值，`scf.if` 变成空 region，语义错误。
2. 如果赋值 RHS 是在 `pto.if_` region 内新产生的 SSA value，则会在后续使用时报 MLIR dominance error。

这和 #973 类似，都是 PTODSL AST rewrite / SSA carry 对 Python rebinding 的处理问题；但这里触发点是 `pto.if_`，不是 `for` loop 里的 list subscript self assignment。

### Reproduction (minimal)

```markdown
Case 1: assignment inside `pto.if_` is silently treated as if it were unconditional


from ptodsl import pto

@pto.jit(name="repro_if_reassign_wrong_semantics", target="a5")
def kernel(n: pto.i32) -> None:
    mask = pto.pset_b32("PAT_ALL")

    x = pto.const(0, dtype=pto.i32)
    with pto.if_((n > 0)) as br, br.then_:
        x = n

    # Expected: vdup uses (n if n > 0 else 0)
    # Actual: vdup uses n unconditionally
    v = pto.vdup(x, mask)
    return

print(kernel.compile().mlir_text())

Actual generated MLIR excerpt:
%1 = arith.cmpi sgt, %arg0, %c0_i32_0 : i32
scf.if %1 {
}
%2 = pto.vdup %arg0, %0 : i32, !pto.mask<b32> -> !pto.vreg<64xi32>

The scf.if is empty, and %arg0 is used unconditionally after the if.

Case 2: assignment to a value created inside pto.if_ causes MLIR dominance failure

from ptodsl import pto

@pto.jit(name="repro_if_reassign_dominance", target="a5")
def kernel(n: pto.i32) -> None:
    mask = pto.pset_b32("PAT_ALL")

    x = pto.const(0, dtype=pto.i32)
    with pto.if_((n > 0)) as br, br.then_:
        x = n + 1

    # Expected: vdup uses if-result (n + 1 if n > 0 else 0)
    # Actual: value from child region is used outside, causing dominance error
    v = pto.vdup(x, mask)
    return

print(kernel.compile().mlir_text())
```

### Expected behavior

Variables reassigned inside pto.if_ should be modeled as values yielded from the scf.if region, similar to:
%new_x = scf.if %cond -> (i32) {
  %then_x = arith.addi %arg0, %c1_i32 : i32
  scf.yield %then_x : i32
} else {
  scf.yield %old_x : i32
}

%v = pto.vdup %new_x, %mask : i32, !pto.mask<b32> -> !pto.vreg<64xi32>

For pto.if_ without an explicit else branch, the else value should preserve the previous value of the variable.

### Actual behavior / error logs

```text
ptoas.mlir._mlir_libs._site_initialize.<locals>.MLIRError: Verification failed:
error: unknown: operand #0 does not dominate this use
 note: unknown: see current operation: %4 = "pto.vdup"(%6, %0) : (i32, !pto.mask<b32>) -> !pto.vreg<64xi32>
 note: unknown: operand defined here (op in a child region)
```

## #1076 [Feature] PTODSL 缺少用于显式 Mixed Kernel 的公共 Cube/Vector Section 接口 【阻塞】

- State: closed
- URL: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/PTOAS/issues/1076
- Created: 2026-07-30T15:37:20Z
- Updated: 2026-08-04T11:54:58Z
- Closed: 2026-08-04T11:54:58Z

### Body

### Summary / 问题背景

PTOAS 后端已经支持以下能力：

- `pto.section.cube` 和 `pto.section.vector` IR。
- 将包含 Cube/Vector Section 的逻辑 Kernel 拆分为对应的物理 Module。
- 生成 Cube/Vector Mixed Fatobj。
- 为同一逻辑 Kernel 生成统一的 Host Stub。

TileLang 的 Mixed Kernel 已经在 TIR 中明确划分了 `CUBE` 和 `VECTOR` Block，因此需要将这两个 Block 映射到 PTOAS 的 Cube/Vector Section。

但 PTODSL 当前没有公开且稳定的接口，用于在同一个显式 Kernel 中直接表达 Cube/Vector Section。



### Motivation / use case / 当前问题

TileLang 目前只能通过以下方式实现 Mixed Kernel，但都不适合作为正式方案：

1. 直接调用 MLIR PTO dialect 的私有接口，创建 `SectionCubeOp` 和 `SectionVectorOp`。
2. 修改 `_compiler._module_spec`、`ModuleStyle` 等 PTODSL 内部状态。
3. 将 Section outline 成 helper，再要求 PTOAS 在 CV split 前进行额外内联。
4. 由 TileLang 自行生成 Cube/Vector 双 Module，并负责公共代码复制、ABI 对齐和 Fatobj 组织。

其中前两种依赖 PTODSL 私有实现；后两种会把本应由 PTOAS/PTODSL 负责的 Mixed Kernel 结构处理转移到 TileLang。

### Proposed API / behavior /  期望能力

希望 PTOAS/PTODSL 提供正式的公共接口，使外部前端能够表达类似以下结构：

```python
@pto.jit(target="a5", mode="explicit")
def kernel(...):
    # Cube/Vector 共用的参数及标量前导计算

    with pto.cube_section():
        # Cube GEMM、L1/L0 搬运及跨核同步

    with pto.vector_section():
        # L0C -> UB -> GM 以及跨核同步
```

该接口需要明确并支持：

- 一个逻辑 Kernel 中同时存在 Cube 和 Vector Section。
- Section 可以使用函数参数以及 Section 外定义的 SSA 值。
- Section 内定义的 SSA 值不得非法逃逸到另一个 Section。
- 不要求调用方修改 `kernel_kind`、`ModuleStyle` 或 compiler 内部状态。
- 生成结果能够直接被 `VPTOSplitCVModule` 和标准 VPTO Pipeline 处理。
- 支持 Mixed Kernel 所需的跨核同步，包括动态 Event ID。
- 明确 Section 采用直接 Region 语义还是 outlined helper 语义。

### Alternatives considered / 验收场景

使用公共 PTODSL API 编写一个 Mixed GEMM Kernel：

- Cube 侧执行 GM/L1/L0 搬运和 GEMM。
- Vector 侧执行 L0C → UB → GM。
- Cube 与 Vector 之间通过跨核 Flag 同步。
- Event ID 可以由运行时标量计算得到。
- Section 外的公共标量可以分别被两个 Section 使用。
- 不依赖任何 PTODSL 私有 Python API。
- 通过标准命令成功生成 Mixed Fatobj：

```bash
ptoas --pto-arch=a5 --pto-backend=vpto kernel.pto -o kernel.o
```


### Additional context / 建议定性

这是一个 PTODSL 公共能力缺口。如果 PTOAS 已经承诺支持基于 Section 的 Mixed Kernel authoring，也可以视为“设计已有但前端实现尚未补齐”的功能性 Bug。

## #1081 [Feature] Remove scalar.cast_index and infer index-to-PTO-scalar conversions in PTODSL

- State: open
- URL: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/PTOAS/issues/1081
- Created: 2026-07-31T04:44:43Z
- Updated: 2026-07-31T04:44:43Z
- Closed: 

### Body

### Summary

希望移除 PTODSL 的 `scalar.cast_index` 公共接口，由 DSL 在需要 PTO scalar 的上下文中自动完成 `index` 到对应 PTO scalar 类型的转换。

当前前端生成或用户编写 PTODSL 时，需要显式插入类似下面的转换：

```python
value = scalar.cast_index(index_value, dtype)
```

这将 MLIR/编译器内部的 `index` 类型适配细节暴露给了 DSL 用户和上游代码生成器。对用户而言，这种转换通常没有业务语义，只是为了满足 PTO op 的 scalar operand 类型要求。

### Motivation / use case

- 简化 PTODSL API，避免用户理解并手动处理 MLIR `index` 与 PTO scalar 类型之间的边界。
- 减少上游前端（例如 TileLang）为每个 scalar operand 特判并生成 `scalar.cast_index` 的代码。
- 让索引表达式可以自然地用于 offset、shape、stride、loop-derived scalar 等参数，同时由 DSL 根据目标 operand 的期望类型完成适配。
- 将转换规则集中在 PTODSL 类型系统/operation builder 中，避免不同调用方使用不一致的 cast 逻辑。

### Proposed API / behavior

当一个 `index` 值传给期望 PTO scalar 类型的 operand 时，PTODSL 应自动插入合法转换。例如：

```python
# Before
pto.some_op(scalar.cast_index(i, pto.i32))

# After
pto.some_op(i)
```

建议的行为边界：

1. 根据 operation schema 中 operand 的期望类型决定目标 scalar 类型，而不是由用户重复指定 dtype。
2. 仅在目标类型明确且转换合法时自动转换；目标类型不明确或存在歧义时给出清晰诊断。
3. 对窄化转换明确规则：如果 `index` 到目标整数类型可能丢失范围信息，应采用项目统一的语义，或要求能够证明安全，否则报错。
4. 保持转换在生成的 PTO/MLIR IR 中显式可见，方便验证和调试；这里只移除用户侧显式 API 调用，并非隐藏 IR cast。
5. 在迁移期可保留 `scalar.cast_index` 并标记 deprecated，待上游调用方迁移后再删除。

### Alternatives considered

继续要求上游前端或 PTODSL 用户显式调用 `scalar.cast_index`。这种方式实现直接，但会把底层类型适配细节扩散到每个调用方，增加生成代码噪音和维护成本，也容易因目标 dtype 选择不一致引入问题。

### Additional context

建议增加以下测试：

- `index` 作为不同 PTO op 的 scalar operand 时能自动转换。
- operation schema 能唯一确定 `i32`/`i64` 等目标类型。
- 类型不明确、非法转换和可能不安全的窄化转换产生明确诊断。
- 已经是正确 PTO scalar 类型的 operand 不产生冗余 cast。
- `scalar.cast_index` 的兼容/弃用路径有覆盖。

验收标准：上游生成的 PTODSL 源码无需出现 `scalar.cast_index`，仍能生成类型合法、转换语义明确的 PTO IR。

## #1083 [Bug] ptoas emits `cache_line_t::...` in CPU sim C++ but `cpu_stub.hpp` exposes legacy global cache constants

- State: closed
- URL: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/PTOAS/issues/1083
- Created: 2026-07-31T08:06:08Z
- Updated: 2026-07-31T09:35:18Z
- Closed: 2026-07-31T09:35:18Z

### Body

## Component

ptoas C++ emission for CPU simulator / `dcci` cache-line arguments.

## Description

When compiling DeepSeek v4-flash sparse attention for `a2a3sim`, ptoas emits CPU simulator C++ that calls:

```cpp
dcci((__gm__ void*)ptr, cache_line_t::SINGLE_CACHE_LINE);
dcci((__gm__ void*)0, cache_line_t::ENTIRE_DATA_CACHE);
```

However the pto-isa CPU stub header currently exposes the legacy global constants:

```cpp
inline constexpr int SINGLE_CACHE_LINE = 0;
inline constexpr int ENTIRE_DATA_CACHE = 0;
inline constexpr int CACHELINE_OUT = 0;
```

from `include/pto/common/cpu_stub.hpp`. There is no `cache_line_t` type in the CPU sim include path, so the generated C++ fails to compile. This looks like a ptoas emission compatibility issue: for CPU sim it should either emit the existing global constants or pto-isa should provide a matching `cache_line_t` definition.

## Reproduction (minimal)

Run with local checkout paths adjusted as needed:

```bash
task-submit --device 7 --run "export PYTHONPATH=<pypto-lib>:<pypto-python>:\$PYTHONPATH && \
export PTOAS_ROOT=<ptoas-0.54>/bin && \
export PTO_ISA_ROOT=<pto-isa> && \
export PTO2_RING_DEP_POOL=524288 && \
export PTO2_RING_TASK_WINDOW=524288 && \
export PTO2_RING_HEAP=2147483648 && \
python <pypto-lib>/models/deepseek/v4-flash/decode_sparse_attn.py --platform a2a3sim"
```

The run generates ptoas inputs and C++ under:

```text
<workdir>/build_output/_jit_sparse_attn_test_*/ptoas/
<workdir>/build_output/_jit_sparse_attn_test_*/kernels/
```

One generated source that reproduces the issue:

```text
<workdir>/build_output/_jit_sparse_attn_test_*/kernels/aiv/csa_slots_build_valid_qk_plan.cpp
```

Relevant generated C++:

```cpp
template <typename Ptr>
static __aicore__ inline void PTOAS__DCCI_SINGLE_CACHE_LINE(Ptr ptr) {
  dcci((__gm__ void*)ptr, cache_line_t::SINGLE_CACHE_LINE);
}

...

dcci((__gm__ void*)0, cache_line_t::ENTIRE_DATA_CACHE);
dsb((mem_dsb_t)0);
```

The corresponding generated PTO input is:

```text
<workdir>/build_output/_jit_sparse_attn_test_*/ptoas/csa_slots_build_valid_qk_plan.pto
```

## Expected behavior

ptoas should emit CPU simulator C++ that compiles against the current pto-isa CPU stub. For the current `cpu_stub.hpp`, the generated code should use the existing global constants, for example:

```cpp
dcci((__gm__ void*)ptr, SINGLE_CACHE_LINE);
dcci((__gm__ void*)0, ENTIRE_DATA_CACHE);
```

or the CPU stub/header contract should be updated consistently so `cache_line_t::SINGLE_CACHE_LINE` and `cache_line_t::ENTIRE_DATA_CACHE` are defined.

## Actual behavior / error logs

```text
[RUN] runtime ...
[SimKernel] Compilation failed: <workdir>/build_output/_jit_sparse_attn_test_*/kernels/aiv/csa_slots_build_valid_qk_plan.cpp: In function 'void PTOAS__DCCI_SINGLE_CACHE_LINE(Ptr)':
<workdir>/build_output/_jit_sparse_attn_test_*/kernels/aiv/csa_slots_build_valid_qk_plan.cpp:48:27: warning: 'cache_line_t' has not been declared [-Wtemplate-body]

## #1086 [Bug] Incorrectly emits PIPE_FIX macro guard in generated AIC kernel

- State: closed
- URL: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/PTOAS/issues/1086
- Created: 2026-07-31T09:06:39Z
- Updated: 2026-08-04T02:35:28Z
- Closed: 2026-08-04T02:35:28Z

### Body

### Component

EmitC / Codegen (lib/PTO/Transforms/PTOToEmitC.cpp)

### Description

PTOAS incorrectly emits the following code when generating an AIC kernel:

```c
#ifndef PIPE_FIX
#define PIPE_FIX PIPE_M
#endif
```
This can redefine PIPE_FIX (PIPE_FIX not exist in system as MACRO) to the wrong pipeline symbol, which causes abnormal AIC pipeline behavior and can make the kernel hang.

[log.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30581523/log.txt)

The macro emission appears to come from:
https://github.com/hw-native-sys/PTOAS/blame/v0.54/lib/PTO/Transforms/PTOToEmitC.cpp#L14671-L14675
Minimal reproducer and generated kernel:
[pipe_fix_issue.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30581089/pipe_fix_issue.py)
[wait_gemm.cpp](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30581090/wait_gemm.cpp)
PyPTO version used for reproduction:
478ddad5a41011645a45019d5196e414c6dc3745

## #1088 [Feature] VMI features to reach CCE parity on FlashAttention and avoid the physical-VPTO workarounds

- State: closed
- URL: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/PTOAS/issues/1088
- Created: 2026-07-31T09:28:45Z
- Updated: 2026-07-31T09:31:57Z
- Closed: 2026-07-31T09:31:57Z

### Body

### Summary

The mixed FlashAttention kernel now reaches ~1.1x CCE cycles in VMI (RVEC 11572 vs
CCE 10482 on cannsim Ascend950), but only by hand-authoring **physical VPTO** ops
(`pto.vexpdif`, `pto.vcvt EVEN/ODD` + `pto.vor` + `pto.vsstb`) that bypass VMI layout
assignment. The idiomatic `pto.vmi.*` form is either ~2.35x slower or fails to
compile in the full kernel. Six PTOAS features would let the clean VMI form both
compile and close the remaining gap:

Cycle-parity levers (the residual ~10%):
1. Scalar-vector multiply lowering (`vmuls` -> hardware `VMULS`, not vector `VMUL`).
2. Direct A5 pipe cross-signals (`sync.set` from `PIPE_MTE1` / `PIPE_V`).
3. Immediate-offset load/store addressing (`VLDI`/`VSTI`).

Authoring / correctness (so the clean VMI form replaces the physical rewrites):
4. Direct `pto.vmi.vexpdif` lowering (no expansion).
5. Compact-narrowing to stride-store layout reconciliation.
6. Fix the plain `pto.vsstb` (no `updated_base`) miscompile.

### Motivation / use case

FlashAttention is compute-and-sync-bound on the Vector pipe; matching the CCE
reference cycle count is the target on cannsim Ascend950 (the CCE run is device-only,
so VMI is the only correct backend). Two fixes already closed the gap from 2.35x to
1.1x (physical NZ-pack + fused `vexpdif`), but both are physical-VPTO hand-rewrites
that sidestep the VMI compiler rather than idiomatic `pto.vmi.*`. The remaining ~10%
and the need for the workarounds are all VMI lowering limitations, not kernel
authoring. Closing them lets any MX / attention kernel be written in clean VMI and
still hit CCE cycles, instead of dropping to physical VPTO per hot loop.

Measured residual (cannsim Ascend950, whole-core / RVEC span):

| Backend | RVEC | vs CCE |
|---|---:|---:|
| CCE (cycle target, device-only) | 10482 | 1.00x |
| VMI (both raw + PTODSL, after fixes) | ~11.6k | ~1.11x |
| VMI before fixes | ~26k | ~2.35x |

### Proposed API / behavior

### 1. Scalar-vector multiply lowering (biggest residual lever)
`pto.vmi.vmuls %v, %scalar` (multiply a vreg by a scalar) currently lowers to a full
vector `VMUL` against a broadcast register. On A5 the hardware `VMULS`
(vector-times-scalar) instruction exists. Trace at the FA scale stage: VMI `VMUL`=1092
vs CCE scalar `VMULS`=516 for the identical arithmetic. Lower `pto.vmi.vmuls` (and the
scalar-operand `vadds`/`vmins`/`vmaxs` family) to the `V*S` scalar-operand form.

### 2. Direct A5 pipe cross-signals
`vmi-v0.1.3`/0.51 accept A5 `pto.sync.set` cross-signals only from `PIPE_FIX` and
`PIPE_MTE3` (`lib/PTO/IR/PTO.cpp:3596` rejects others). The kernel therefore inserts
bridge signals `MTE1 -> FIX` and `V -> MTE3`, which amplify the MTE3 wait count
(VMI 17 vs CCE 5). Allow `sync.set` directly from `PIPE_MTE1` and `PIPE_V` on A5 (as
CCE emits) so the bridges and their extra waits disappear.

### 3. Immediate-offset load/store addressing
VMI emits register-offset `RV_VLD` / `RV_VST` where CCE emits immediate-offset
`VLDI` / `VSTI`. Counts and per-op cost are currently identical (2524 loads / 1810
stores each; VLD 9.5 vs VLDI 9.7 avg), so this is cycle-neutral today, but it forces
extra scalar address arithmetic and diverges from the CCE instruction shape. Emitting
immediate-offset addressing where the offset is a compile-time constant matches CCE
and reduces the scalar/address footprint.

### 4. Direct `pto.vmi.vexpdif` lowering (see ptoas_gaps.md Gap 1)
`pto.vmi.vexpdif %scores, %max, %mask` is expanded to `[extf] -> subf -> exp` before
layout assignment (`lib/PTO/Transforms/VMILowerUnifiedToLegacy.cpp:1045-1069`,
installed unconditionally in `tools/ptoas/ptoas.cpp:2772`). The fused physical
`pto.vexpdif` exists and is emitted (`VPTOOps.td:3287`,
`VPTOCANN900LLVMEmitter.cpp:3814`). Lower `pto.vmi.vexpdif` directly to `pto.vexpdif`
instead of expanding. Removes 516 net RVEC ops AND removes the need to hand-author the
physical op in the kernel.

### 5. Compact-narrowing to stride-store layout reconciliation (see Gap 2)
The clean pack `pto.vmi.vcvt fp32 -> bf16 {SAT}` then `pto.vmi.vstore(stride 65,1)`
compiles in an isolated probe but fails in the full inlined `simd_vf_2`: layout
assignment pins `lane_stride=2` on the vcvt output, which `stride_store` rejects
(`VMI-LAYOUT-CONTRACT: ... lane_stride = 2 but requires contiguous`;
`ensure_layout has no registered materialization`). Provide ONE of:
- constraint propagation so `stride_store` forces compact (contiguous) narrowing on
  its producer,
- a registered `lane_stride=2 -> contiguous` ensure_layout materialization, or
- a public VMI annotation to force compact narrowing output.
Any of these lets the idiomatic pack compile without the UB-staging round trip or the
physical `vcvt EVEN/ODD + vor + vsstb` rewrite.

### 6. Fix the plain `pto.vsstb` miscompile (see Gap 4)
The plain `pto.vsstb` form (no `updated_base` result) produces wrong NZ output
(max_rel 2.16) in the full kernel; only the `post_update = POST_UPDATE` form (matching
the `-> !pto.ptr` result and the CCE reference) is correct. Either fix the plain form
or reject it at verification so it cannot silently miscompile.

### Alternatives considered

- **Physical-VPTO hand-rewrites (applied).** We closed 2.35x -> 1.1x by writing the
  NZ pack and the exp-difference as physical VPTO in both the raw `.pto` and the
  PTODSL kernel. This works and is correct, but it bypasses the VMI compiler per hot
  loop, is not portable to other kernels, and does not address features 1-3 (the
  residual 10% is still there because those are lowering choices, not kernel edits).
- **UB staging round trip for the pack (original).** Store narrowed value to UB,
  barrier, reload, then stride-store. Correct on stock VMI but ~4332 vs 776 cycles in
  `simd_vf_2` (the entire original gap). Rejected.
- **Leaving `pto.vmi.vmuls` as vector `VMUL`.** Numerically fine, but doubles the
  scale-stage op count vs CCE with no benefit.

### Additional context

[fa_mix_vmi.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30582467/fa_mix_vmi.zip)

## #1092 bug(vpto): non-zero pto.vci / llvm.hivm.vci base ignored on A5 camodel

- State: closed
- URL: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/PTOAS/issues/1092
- Created: 2026-07-31T16:35:45Z
- Updated: 2026-08-13T08:52:56Z
- Closed: 2026-08-13T08:52:56Z

### Body

## Summary
On Ascend950PR camodel (Bisheng + `llvm.hivm.vci`), a **non-zero scalar base** passed to `pto.vci` is ignored. The hardware/backend always behaves as `vci(0)` and emits lane ids `[0..N)`, even when LLVM IR correctly carries the base immediate.

This breaks absolute index generation such as `vci(i * 64)` for multi-vreg expert indexing (e.g. TileLang `topk_gate`).

## Spec expectation
For ASC order:

```text
result[i] = base + i
```

So `pto.vci %c64` on `!pto.vreg<64xi32>` should yield `[64, 65, ..., 127]`.

## Observed
Camodel returns `[0, 1, ..., 63]`.

End-to-end symptom in TileLang topk_gate (E=384): top-1 expert **144** was reported as **16** (`144 % 64`), and **292** as **36**, until indices were materialized as `vci(0) + vadds(base)`.

## Minimal repro (legacy VPTO)

```mlir
// kernel.pto — expected [64..127], observed [0..63]
module attributes {pto.target_arch = "a5", pto.backend = "vpto"} {
  func.func @vci_nonzero_base(%arg0: !pto.ptr<i32, gm>)
      attributes {pto.entry, pto.kernel_kind = #pto.kernel_kind<vector>} {
    %c0_i64 = arith.constant 0 : i64
    %ub = pto.castptr %c0_i64 : i64 -> !pto.ptr<i32, ub>
    %c0 = arith.constant 0 : index
    %c64_i32 = arith.constant 64 : i32
    pto.vecscope {
      %mask = pto.pset_b32 "PAT_ALL" : !pto.mask<b32>
      %idx = pto.vci %c64_i32 {order = "ASC"} : i32 -> !pto.vreg<64xi32>
      pto.vsts %idx, %ub[%c0], %mask
        : !pto.vreg<64xi32>, !pto.ptr<i32, ub>, !pto.mask<b32>
    }
    pto.set_flag["PIPE_V", "PIPE_MTE3", "EVENT_ID0"]
    pto.wait_flag["PIPE_V", "PIPE_MTE3", "EVENT_ID0"]
    %c1 = arith.constant 1 : i64
    %c64 = arith.constant 64 : i64
    %c0b = arith.constant 0 : i64
    pto.set_loop_size_ubtoout %c1, %c1 : i64, i64
    pto.copy_ubuf_to_gm %ub, %arg0, %c0b, %c1, %c64, %c0b, %c64, %c64
      : !pto.ptr<i32, ub>, !pto.ptr<i32, gm>, i64, i64, i64, i64, i64, i64
    pto.barrier #pto.pipe<PIPE_ALL>
    return
  }
}
```

PTOAS still emits the base into LLVM correctly:

```llvm
declare <64 x i32> @llvm.hivm.vci.v64s32(i32, i32)
%7 = call <64 x i32> @llvm.hivm.vci.v64s32(i32 64, i32 0)
```

So this looks like a **Bisheng / HIVM intrinsic / camodel** bug (or undocumented encoding) rather than PTOAS dropping the operand in IR.

## VMI form
`pto.vmi.vci %c64` (size 64, contiguous) currently lowers through contiguous iota to a single `pto.vci %c64`, which hits the same backend bug.

## Workaround
Materialize absolute indices as:

```text
lanes = vci(0)
result = vadds(lanes, base)   # or ASC: vci(0)+vadds; DESC: vdup(base)-vci(0)
```

TileLang ASC already used `vci(0) + vadds(i*64)` for this reason. A local PTOAS workaround rewrites contiguous VMI iota the same way; ideally the backend honors the intrinsic base so that rewrite can be removed.

## Environment
- Soc: `Ascend950PR_9599` camodel via `msprof op simulator`
- PTOAS built against llvm-vpto (HIVM) + CANN 9.0.0
- Reproduced via TileLang `examples/ascend/vmi/topk_gate` before the `vci(0)+vadds` rewrite

## Ask
1. Confirm whether `llvm.hivm.vci.*(base, order)` is supposed to honor a non-zero `base`.
2. If yes, fix Bisheng/HIVM lowering / camodel so `vci(64)` yields `[64..127]`.
3. If the intrinsic is lane-only by design, please document that and keep the `vci(0)+vadds(base)` materialization as the supported pattern (and update ISA docs / gym cases that pass non-zero bases).

## #1095 [Bug] PTODSL 可变变量会导致 SSA 值跨物理 Section 泄漏【阻塞】

- State: closed
- URL: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/PTOAS/issues/1095
- Created: 2026-08-01T06:49:12Z
- Updated: 2026-08-05T07:39:12Z
- Closed: 2026-08-05T07:39:12Z

### Body

### Component

Python bindings (python/)

### Description

PTODSL 当前使用同一个 Python 可变变量环境，依次追踪相邻的
`pto.section("cube")` 和 `pto.section("vector")`。

当一个 Python 变量在某个物理 Section 内被重新赋值后，该变量可能会指向
这个 Section 内部定义的 SSA 值。后续追踪相邻 Section 时，可能错误地继续
使用这个 SSA 值。

这违反了物理 Section 之间的隔离要求。Cube 和 Vector Section 最终会被
拆分为不同的物理 Kernel，因此一个 Section 内定义的 SSA 值不能被另一个
Section 引用。

该问题主要在 mixed Cube/Vector Kernel（`mixed=true`）中暴露，因为其中的
Cube 和 Vector Section 会被拆分为不同的物理区域或函数。在普通的单 Section
Kernel 中，代码位于同一个顺序执行区域，正常的 SSA 支配关系可能会掩盖这个问题。

期望的 Section 语义如下：

- 函数根作用域定义的值可以作为入口值被任意物理 Section 使用。
- 在某个 Section 内对 Python 可变变量的重新赋值，只能影响该 Section。
- 在物理 Section 内定义的值不能逃逸到相邻 Section 或函数根作用域。
- 非法的跨 Section SSA 引用应在 Split CV 之前被明确诊断，而不是生成错误的
  物理 Kernel。

建议采用多层防护方案：

1. PTODSL AST rewrite 将 `pto.section()` 视为独立的变量作用域边界。
2. 每个物理 Section 使用函数根作用域提供的入口值独立追踪，而不是继承前一个
   Section 追踪结束后的 Python 可变状态。
3. PTODSL tracing 检查 Section 内定义的 surface value 是否发生逃逸，包括关闭
   AST rewrite 的情况。
4. PTOAS Split CV pass 增加跨 Section SSA 校验，同时覆盖 operation result 和
   block argument。



### Reproduction (minimal)

```markdown
from ptodsl import pto


@pto.jit(target="a5", mode="explicit")
def section_scope_repro():
    event_id = pto.const(1, dtype=pto.i32)
    one = pto.const(1, dtype=pto.i32)

    with pto.section("cube"):
        event_id = event_id + one
        pto.wait_flag("S", "MTE2", event_id=event_id)

    with pto.section("vector"):
        # 这里应该使用根作用域的入口值 1，
        # 而不是 Cube Section 内定义的值 2。
        pto.wait_flag("MTE2", "S", event_id=event_id)


print(section_scope_repro.compile().mlir_text())



python section_scope_repro.py


问题 IR 在语义上相当于：


%root = ... : i32
pto.section.cube {
  %cube_value = arith.addi %root, %root : i32
  // ...
}
pto.section.vector {
  // 非法：%cube_value 定义在相邻的 Cube Section 中。
  "some.op"(%cube_value) : (i32) -> ()
}
```

### Expected behavior


```text
每个物理 Section 都应从函数根作用域的入口状态开始执行。

在上述示例中，Cube Section 可以在自身内部生成并使用 event_id = 2，但
Vector Section 应独立使用根作用域定义的 event_id = 1。

如果代码直接在另一个物理 Section 或函数根作用域中使用某个 Section 内定义的
SSA 值，应在编译期间给出清晰的错误诊断。
```

### Actual behavior / error logs

```text
追踪 Cube Section 时，对 event_id 的重新赋值修改了共享的 Python 变量环境。
随后追踪 Vector Section 时，event_id 仍然指向 Cube Section 内生成的 SSA 值。

PTODSL 没有阻止该值逃逸，因此跨 Section 的 SSA 引用能够进入 Split CV
转换。Section 被拆分后，对应 SSA 值并没有定义在生成的物理 Kernel 中，从而
产生非法 IR 或错误的生成代码。
```

### Git commit

9d0d6a50af84d5c3277287fcc3d12ccbd2f9e97c

### Host platform

Linux (x86_64)

### Target Ascend arch (if relevant)

a5

### PTOAS build level (if relevant)

None

### 关联ISSUE & PR
此问题发现基于PR #1041 
关联ISSUE #1076

## #1097 [Bug][阻塞] PTODSL's `for` loop incorrectly carries variables initialized inside `pto.vecscope()`

PTODSL

### Description

PTODSL 中，若 `for ... in range(...)` 循环中包含 `pto.vecscope()` 块，完全在 `pto.vecscope()` 内声明并读写的变量会被暴露到 `for` 循环中，成为循环内携带（carry）的变量

print(kernel.compile().mlir_text())

编译成功通过

## #1102 [Bug] [PTODSL] [阻塞] `pto.vdup` 无法处理 `ui16/ui32` 标量，生成的 operand 与 result 类型不一致

- State: closed
- URL: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/PTOAS/issues/1102
- Created: 2026-08-03T02:17:38Z
- Updated: 2026-08-07T06:40:05Z
- Closed: 2026-08-07T06:40:05Z

### Body

### Component

Python bindings (python/)

### Description

PTODSL 的 `pto.vdup` 接口声明支持以下整数标量类型：

- `i8/i16/i32`
- `si8/si16/si32`
- `ui8/ui16/ui32`

但当输入是带类型的 `ui16` 或 `ui32` 标量时，PTODSL 生成的 `pto.vdup` operand 保留 unsigned 类型，而 result vector 被规范化为 signless integer，导致 MLIR verifier 报错：

```text
'pto.vdup' op scalar input must match result element type

### Reproduction (minimal)

```markdown
from ptodsl import pto


@pto.jit(
    name="vdup_ui16_repro",
    kernel_kind="vector",
    target="a5",
    mode="explicit",
)
def vdup_ui16_repro():
    mask = pto.pset_b16("PAT_ALL")
    pto.vdup(pto.const(32512, dtype=pto.ui16), mask)


@pto.jit(
    name="vdup_ui32_repro",
    kernel_kind="vector",
    target="a5",
    mode="explicit",
)
def vdup_ui32_repro():
    mask = pto.pset_b32("PAT_ALL")
    pto.vdup(pto.const(2147483648, dtype=pto.ui32), mask)


for name, kernel in (
    ("vdup_ui16_repro", vdup_ui16_repro),
    ("vdup_ui32_repro", vdup_ui32_repro),
):
    print(f"=== {name} ===")
    try:
        kernel.compile()
        print("PASS")
    except Exception as exc:
        print(type(exc).__name__)
        print(exc)
```

### Expected behavior

pto.vdup 应能接受其接口声明支持的 ui8/ui16/ui32 标量。
由于 PTO integer vreg 的元素类型使用 signless integer，PTODSL 应在构造 VdupOp 前，将带 signedness 的整数标量规范化为相同位宽的 signless integer，同时保持原始位模式。
例如：
```text
ui16 -> i16
ui32 -> i32
```
转换后，pto.vdup 的 scalar operand 和 result element type 应完全一致。

### Actual behavior / error logs

```text
=== vdup_ui16_repro ===
MLIRError
Verification failed:
error: unknown: 'pto.vdup' op scalar input must match result element type
 note: unknown: see current operation:
 %4 = "pto.vdup"(%2, %0)
     : (ui16, !pto.mask<b16>) -> !pto.vreg<128xi16>

=== vdup_ui32_repro ===
MLIRError
Verification failed:
error: unknown: 'pto.vdup' op scalar input must match result element type
 note: unknown: see current operation:
 %4 = "pto.vdup"(%2, %0)
     : (ui32, !pto.mask<b32>) -> !pto.vreg<64xi32>
```

## #1106 [Pass Bug] level3 alloc_multi_tile fan-out addresses are not constant-folded, so multi-buffer sync degrades to single-buffer

- State: closed
- URL: https://github.com/hw-native-sys/PTOAS/issues/1106
- Created: 2026-08-03T07:10:11Z
- Updated: 2026-08-06T01:14:34Z
- Closed: 2026-08-06T01:14:34Z

### Body

## Summary

Under `--pto-level=level3`, `pto.alloc_multi_tile addr = %base` fans the base out into a
multi-address `pto.pointer_cast`, but slot k's address is emitted as an **unfolded**
`arith.addi %base, %c<k*slotBytes>` instead of a constant. Per the multi-buffer design
(`docs/designs/ptoas-multi-buffer-explicit-design.md` §5.4.1), a `pointer_cast` whose
address list contains a non-constant operand falls back to the conservative path
(`rootBuffer = addr0`, `baseAddresses = {0}`), so all slot narrowing is lost.

Consequence: at level3 the whole multi-buffer feature degrades to single-buffer sync.

- **Dynamic slot** (`%k = arith.remui %i, %c2`): no dyn event ids at all — one static
  `EVENT_ID0`, load and consume fully serialized. level2 on the same input emits two
  primed event ids + `set_flag_dyn` / `wait_flag_dyn`.
- **Constant slots** (`%mb[0]` / `%mb[1]`): *worse than not using multi-buffer* — the two
  slots are treated as one buffer, so an extra false MTE3→MTE2 WAR pair appears that two
  plain `pto.alloc_tile`s with constant addresses do not produce.

This blocks PyPTO: when PyPTO owns local-memory planning it always invokes ptoas at
`--pto-level=level3`, so today adopting `alloc_multi_tile` / `multi_tile_get` there is a
net regression, and the feature is only usable via the ptoas memory planner (level2).

## Pass / pipeline name

`pto-view-to-memref` (level3 explicit-addr fan-out); observable in `pto-insert-sync` and
the graph sync solver.

## Command line

```bash
# dynamic slot
ptoas mb_l3.pto -o mb_l3.cpp --enable-insert-sync --pto-level=level3 --pto-arch=a3
ptoas mb_l2.pto -o mb_l2.cpp --enable-insert-sync --pto-level=level2 --pto-arch=a3  # reference

# constant slots
ptoas cs_multi_l3.pto -o cs_multi_l3.cpp --enable-insert-sync --pto-level=level3 --pto-arch=a3
ptoas cs_plain_l3.pto -o cs_plain_l3.cpp --enable-insert-sync --pto-level=level3 --pto-arch=a3  # reference
```

`--enable-graph-sync-solver` instead of `--enable-insert-sync` behaves the same.

## Before IR (input)

### A. Dynamic slot, level3 (`mb_l3.pto`)

```mlir
module {
  func.func @prefetch_dyn_eid_l3(
      %gm : memref<16x16xf16, #pto.address_space<gm>>,
      %dst : memref<16x16xf16, #pto.address_space<gm>>,
      %n : index) attributes {pto.entry} {
    %c0 = arith.constant 0 : index
    %c1 = arith.constant 1 : index
    %c2 = arith.constant 2 : index
    %base = arith.constant 32768 : i64

    %mb = pto.alloc_multi_tile addr = %base
        : !pto.multi_tile_buf<vec, 16x16xf16, count=2>

    scf.for %i = %c0 to %n step %c1 {
      %idx = arith.remui %i, %c2 : index
      %prod = pto.multi_tile_get %mb[%idx]
          : !pto.multi_tile_buf<vec, 16x16xf16, count=2>
         -> !pto.tile_buf<vec, 16x16xf16>
      pto.tload ins(%gm : memref<16x16xf16, #pto.address_space<gm>>)
                outs(%prod : !pto.tile_buf<vec, 16x16xf16>)
      pto.tstore ins(%prod : !pto.tile_buf<vec, 16x16xf16>)
                 outs(%dst : memref<16x16xf16, #pto.address_space<gm>>)
    }
    return
  }
}
```

The level2 reference (`mb_l2.pto`) is the same module with `addr = %base` and the `%base`
constant removed.

### B. Constant slots, level3 (`cs_multi_l3.pto`)

```mlir
module {
  func.func @cs_multi(%gm0 : memref<16x16xf16, #pto.address_space<gm>>,
                      %gm1 : memref<16x16xf16, #pto.address_space<gm>>,
                      %dst : memref<16x16xf16, #pto.address_space<gm>>) attributes {pto.entry} {
    %c0 = arith.constant 0 : index
    %c1 = arith.constant 1 : index
    %base = arith.constant 32768 : i64
    %mb = pto.alloc_multi_tile addr = %base : !pto.multi_tile_buf<vec, 16x16xf16, count=2>
    %s0 = pto.multi_tile_get %mb[%c0] : !pto.multi_tile_buf<vec, 16x16xf16, count=2> -> !pto.tile_buf<vec, 16x16xf16>
    %s1 = pto.multi_tile_get %mb[%c1] : !pto.multi_tile_buf<vec, 16x16xf16, count=2> -> !pto.tile_buf<vec, 16x16xf16>
    pto.tload  ins(%gm0 : memref<16x16xf16, #pto.address_space<gm>>) outs(%s0 : !pto.tile_buf<vec, 16x16xf16>)
    pto.tstore ins(%s0 : !pto.tile_buf<vec, 16x16xf16>) outs(%dst : memref<16x16xf16, #pto.address_space<gm>>)
    pto.tload  ins(%gm1 : memref<16x16xf16, #pto.address_space<gm>>) outs(%s1 : !pto.tile_buf<vec, 16x16xf16>)
    pto.tstore ins(%s1 : !pto.tile_buf<vec, 16x16xf16>) outs(%dst : memref<16x16xf16, #pto.address_space<gm>>)
    return
  }
}
```

The reference (`cs_plain_l3.pto`) replaces the multi-buffer with two plain allocs:

```mlir
    %a0 = arith.constant 32768 : i64
    %a1 = arith.constant 33280 : i64
    %s0 = pto.alloc_tile addr = %a0 : !pto.tile_buf<vec, 16x16xf16>
    %s1 = pto.alloc_tile addr = %a1 : !pto.tile_buf<vec, 16x16xf16>
```

## Expected behavior

level3 should reach the same sync quality as level2 for the same slot expressions — the
slot addresses are compile-time constants in both cases, the only difference is who
computed them.

- Case A: two primed event ids + `set_flag_dyn` / `wait_flag_dyn` keyed off the slot SSA
  (as `test/lit/pto/multi_tile_prefetch_dyn_event_id.pto` checks at the default level).
- Case B: slots 0 and 1 have disjoint `baseAddresses`, so no sync between them — the same
  sequence the two-plain-`alloc_tile` reference produces.

## Actual IR or error

IR after `pto-view-to-memref` at level3 (case A) — slot 1's address is an unfolded `addi`:

```text
%c32768_i64 = arith.constant 32768 : i64
%c512_i64 = arith.constant 512 : i64
%0 = arith.addi %c32768_i64, %c512_i64 : i64
%1 = pto.pointer_cast(%c32768_i64, %0) %c16, %c16_0 {config = ...} : memref<16x16xf16, ...>
%2 = pto.bind_tile %1, ...
scf.for %arg3 = %c0 to %arg2 step %c1 {
  %3 = arith.remui %arg3, %c2 : index
  %4 = pto.slot_marker %2[%3] : ...
  ...
}
```

Emitted C++, case A at **level3** (single static event id, serialized):

```text
set_flag(PIPE_MTE3, PIPE_MTE2, EVENT_ID0);
  wait_flag(PIPE_MTE3, PIPE_MTE2, EVENT_ID0);
  set_flag(PIPE_MTE2, PIPE_MTE3, EVENT_ID0);
  wait_flag(PIPE_MTE2, PIPE_MTE3, EVENT_ID0);
  set_flag(PIPE_MTE3, PIPE_MTE2, EVENT_ID0);
wait_flag(PIPE_MTE3, PIPE_MTE2, EVENT_ID0);
```

Same module at **level2** (correct — two event ids, dynamic ids `v14` / `v21`):

```text
set_flag(PIPE_MTE3, PIPE_MTE2, EVENT_ID0);
set_flag(PIPE_MTE3, PIPE_MTE2, EVENT_ID1);
  wait_flag(PIPE_MTE3, PIPE_MTE2, v14);
  set_flag(PIPE_MTE2, PIPE_MTE3, EVENT_ID0);
  wait_flag(PIPE_MTE2, PIPE_MTE3, EVENT_ID0);
  set_flag(PIPE_MTE3, PIPE_MTE2, v21);
wait_flag(PIPE_MTE3, PIPE_MTE2, EVENT_ID0);
wait_flag(PIPE_MTE3, PIPE_MTE2, EVENT_ID1);
```

Case B at level3 — diff of the sync/op sequence, `cs_plain_l3.cpp` → `cs_multi_l3.cpp`.
The multi-buffer version has one *extra* false WAR pair between slot 0's store and
slot 1's load:

```text
> set_flag(PIPE_MTE3, PIPE_MTE2, EVENT_ID0);
> wait_flag(PIPE_MTE3, PIPE_MTE2, EVENT_ID0);
```

## Suggested fix

In the level3 explicit-addr path of `PTOViewToMemref`, fold `base + k * slotBytes` when
`base` is a constant (both operands are constants by construction), so the fan-out
produces N literal `arith.constant` addresses — the shape `PTOPlanMemory` already produces
at level1/level2. Alternatively, run a canonicalize/fold before the InsertSync and GSS IR
translators so `UpdatePointerCastOpMemInfo` sees constants.

A regression test could extend `test/lit/pto/multi_tile_level3_explicit_addr.pto` with a
`CHECK` that the fan-out addresses are constants, plus a level3 variant of
`multi_tile_prefetch_dyn_event_id.pto`.

## Version

`ptoas 0.54` (installed binary `/usr/local/ptoas/0.54/bin/ptoas`); local source checkout
at `4259f31e915af45ac7365aea514d2cfd6aff0103`. Reproduced identically with
`--enable-insert-sync` and `--enable-graph-sync-solver`.

- Arch: a3
- PTOAS build level: level3
